In a recent development, available on both iOS and Android, the Direct app largely mirrors Instagram’s texting feature. It sounds similar to Meta’s Messenger app, which itself spun out of Facebook for texts and video calls. And it would also join WhatsApp, so the organization certainly has no shortage of different ways to text.

The Direct app includes several features for personalizing your conversations, including drawing, custom stickers, voice effects and chat background themes. You can also use it with or without an Instagram account, which could be particularly useful for someone who wants to text someone on the platform but intentionally doesn’t want a profile on the service. When using the service without a full Instagram account, you can add others by username or by scanning a QR code.

In a recent development, across Meta’s chat apps, the company has taken different approaches to end-to-end encryption and privacy. Instagram’s conversations aren’t presently encrypted, whereas those on Messenger and WhatsApp are.

In a recent development, meta indicates the Direct app will require people to verify their age and will use technology to block anyone under 13 from using the chat app. The service will also provide similar protections for teen accounts as are right now offered in the main Instagram app.

Is Investing in an S&P 500 ETF Really Enough? Here's My Honest Take.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • 10 stocks we like better than Vanguard S&P 500 ETF ›.
  • Industry observers note that exchange-traded funds are a great way to gain exposure to many stocks at once -- and one that tracks the S&P 500 could be particularly interesting.
  • A look at the famous benchmark's performance over the past three calendar years also is reason to give us confidence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adria Cimino – Nov 19, 2026 at 5:02AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Vanguard S&P 500 ETF ›.

Industry observers note that exchange-traded funds are a great way to gain exposure to many stocks at once -- and one that tracks the S&P 500 could be particularly interesting. After all, the S&P 500 has been a winning investment over time, delivering an average annual return of 10% since the index's launch in the late 1950s.

A look at the famous benchmark's performance over the past three calendar years also is reason to give us confidence. It's climbed 78% over that time period as the bull market advanced -- and even amid certain headwinds this year, the S&P 500 is heading for a gain.

In a recent development, so, is investing in an S&P 500 ETF really enough? Here's my honest take.

In a recent development, first, let's talk a bit about ETF investing. As mentioned, these assets allow you to gain exposure to many stocks, and this is according to a theme such as biotech or retail, or an ETF may reflect the performance of an index. In each case, ETFs offer a certain degree of diversification.

According to recent reports, and with diversification in mind, an S&P 500 ETF, such as the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO +0.91%), is an excellent choice. This is because the major index is well-diversified across 11 industries, so an ETF that tracks it will have the same composition. Of course, today, tech stocks are heavily weighted in the S&P 500, so they more heavily influence performance than an industry with a lower weighting, such as utilities. But this may change over time as the composition of the index evolves.

And this brings me to my next point: By investing in an S&P 500 ETF, you'll always be exposed to the key companies driving the day's economy. This is because the major index rebalances on a quarterly basis, removing companies that no longer meet membership criteria and adding new ones that do. ETFs that track the index must follow these moves, and as a result, investors benefit from the growth of the day's most significant industries and companies.

NYSEMKT · As of 9:39 AM ET 11/19/26.

Finally, an S&P 500 ETF is a low-maintenance investment: You can invest and hold over time without closely inspecting earnings reports or corporate comments.

According to recent reports, one thing to keep in mind is that ETFs come with fees, expressed as an expense ratio, so you'll want to go for one with a ratio of less than 1% to optimize your gains. The Vanguard S&P 500 ETF, with an expense ratio of 0.03%, fits the bill. And ETFs trade daily on the market just like stocks, so they're easy to buy and sell.

Considering all of this, you might think that all you really need is an S&P 500 ETF. But is investing in such an asset enough? Here's my honest take. ETF investing is fantastic for all of the reasons I've mentioned above. And an S&P 500 ETF is a great fit for any investment style -- from cautious to aggressive.

In a recent development, but I wouldn't stop my investing story right here. It's vital to also buy individual stocks, as they can truly supercharge your performance over time. Though a company like Apple is the heaviest-weighted in the S&P 500, and therefore in the funds that track it, you can benefit more from Apple's gains by directly holding it than from holding an index fund. For example, Apple is heading for a 29% gain this year, while the S&P 500 is advancing about 8%. And over time, the difference can be greater too, with Apple and the S&P 500 rising 133% and 57%, respectively, over the past five years.

Industry observers note that so it's wise to buy an S&P 500 index fund, but in my honest opinion, investors shouldn't stop there. According to your investing style and comfort with risk, you should also build out a broad portfolio including quality individual stocks. An S&P 500 ETF and a mix of solid stocks are complementary and together could help you build wealth over the long term.

Solidarietà a Claudio Lotito per le intimidazioni ricevute, ma anche un invito al presidente della Lazio a compiere un passo verso quella parte della tifoseria che si sente tradita. Alessandro Onorato interviene nel momento delicato del rapporto tra il patron biancoceleste e i sostenitori laziali.

L'assessore allo Sport di Roma Capitale parla anche dello sciopero del tifo e rivela di continuare ad andare allo stadio insieme alle figlie. Sullo sfondo c'è poi un altro tema centrale per il futuro della Lazio: il Flaminio. Secondo Onorato, l'iter potrebbe arrivare alla dichiarazione di interesse pubblico entro Natale, a determinate condizioni.

Secondo quanto riportato da Il Foglio, Onorato ha affrontato i diversi temi partendo proprio dalle intimidazioni indirizzate a Lotito.

“Le intimidazioni a Lotito? Intollerabili e ingiustificabili, persino con minacce di morte al figlio, gli sono solidale e penso faccia bene ad avere il coraggio di andare contro chi utilizza la curva per fare pressioni indebite. Lo sciopero del tifo? Quando ho tempo, io allo stadio ci vado insieme alle mie figlie: non vorrei che perdessero la passione per il biancazzurro, penso però che il presidente debba fare uno sforzo verso centinaia di migliaia di tifosi per bene”.

Onorato non intende entrare direttamente nella polemica calcistica tra Claudio Lotito e i tifosi della Lazio.

“Da uomo delle istituzioni farei una cosa inopportuna”.

L'assessore sottolinea però un elemento particolare del momento attraversato dal club:.

“È un peccato che ci sia questa protesta proprio ora che la Lazio è prima in classifica”.

Onorato distingue inoltre la posizione degli ultrà da quella di altri sostenitori che hanno scelto di non andare allo stadio:.

“C’è anche tanta gente, non ultrà, che non va allo stadio perché si sente tradita da Lotito. Verso queste persone sarebbe bello se il presidente facesse un gesto di distensione. La stragrande maggioranza delle persone sane che amano la Lazio in questo momento sta soffrendo. È evidente che serve anche alla società distinguere tra il tifo malato e quello sano”.

It has been revealed that nella protesta è intervenuto anche il presidente della Regione Lazio Francesco Rocca. Una scelta che Onorato non avrebbe compiuto:.

“Fossi stato in lui non sarei entrato in questa polemica. Penso sia una questione interna alla destra che però danneggia la comunità del tifo laziale”.

Allo stesso tempo, l'assessore riconosce a Lotito un merito preciso risalente all'inizio della sua presidenza:.

Sources indicate that “Lotito ha avuto il grande merito, sin dall’inizio della sua presidenza alla Lazio, nel 2004, di distinguere con nettezza la parte sana del tifo dalle infiltrazioni criminali. Anche per questo sarebbe bello che oggi tendesse una mano verso i primi per superare un clima che fa solo male alla squadra: un calcio senza tifosi è davvero triste”.

Industry observers note that non si tratta, secondo Onorato, di una difesa politica del senatore di Forza Italia. Il problema avrebbe infatti dimensioni molto più ampie.

According to recent reports, “Non è questo. Non è un problema che riguarda solo la Lazio. Mi chiedo perché il governo Meloni non faccia qualcosa di veramente incisivo per intervenire su tantissimi gruppi ultrà che hanno interessi illeciti e tendono a fare pressioni indebite sulle presidenze. Non solo su Lotito, ma penso a quello che è avvenuto al Lecce, all’Inter, al Milan, alla Juve o in altri comuni con squadre più piccole. Avere il coraggio di prendere le distanze da questi gruppi organizzati nel calcio di oggi è molto complesso. Anche perché le contiguità con la destra sono note”.

Onorato torna anche su una delle prime decisioni adottate da Lotito da presidente della Lazio, quando tolse il merchandising agli Irriducibili.

It has been revealed that “E fece benissimo. Se vogliamo un calcio all’altezza delle sfide internazionali, il merchandising deve essere appannaggio delle società. È una voce importante che consente ai club di realizzare ricavi che possono poi essere reinvestiti nella crescita della squadra”.

Altro capitolo importante riguarda il nuovo stadio della Lazio e il progetto di riqualificazione del Flaminio.

In questo caso Onorato mette da parte qualsiasi appartenenza politica o sportiva:.

“Su questo non ci sono colori politici, né sportivi: faccio quello che mi spetta da assessore”.

L'assessore giudica positivamente il lavoro presentato dalla Lazio e spiega a che punto si trova il procedimento:.

According to recent reports, “Posso però senz’altro dire che il progetto è molto avanzato e, a differenza di quanto detto da tanti, è un progetto serio. Si è conclusa la prima conferenza dei servizi, con alcuni rilievi della Sovrintendenza statale, ai quali la Lazio ha risposto. Adesso stiamo aspettando che risponda a sua volta il ministero per poter completare l’iter”.

I prossimi passaggi potrebbero risultare decisivi e Onorato indica anche una possibile tempistica:.

“Se nei prossimi giorni la Sovrintendenza risponde e la Lazio adegua il progetto e il piano economico-finanziario, noi entro Natale possiamo chiudere l’iter per arrivare alla dichiarazione di interesse pubblico”.

Microsoft blames major outage on a July patch defect – and two other factors

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (886 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Microsoft has released newly introduced information explaining the massive outage that started Thursday morning and affected Microsoft 365, Copilot, and Outlook access in 74 countries, according to Downdetector.
  • In a recent development, charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents, and Platform, posted early Monday morning that the outage was due to three factors, including a “latent defect” from a July revision to Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers.
  • “A latent defect caused servers to become overwhelmed and unresponsive under certain load conditions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Microsoft has released newly introduced information explaining the massive outage that started Thursday morning and affected Microsoft 365, Copilot, and Outlook access in 74 countries, according to Downdetector.

In a recent development, charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents, and Platform, posted early Monday morning that the outage was due to three factors, including a “latent defect” from a July revision to Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers. Low server capacity and peak traffic in the US brought the defect out of hiding, despite no prior reported issues.

“A latent defect caused servers to become overwhelmed and unresponsive under certain load conditions. This was due to lock contention inside an internal process which caused the machine to become unavailable,” Lamanna said, noting that the enhancement was deployed safely worldwide without any issues for over three months.

He said Microsoft didn’t find the glitch in testing due to “the different traffic and SKU mix used in our test labs,” because “our load testing tended to focus on our weaker hardware SKUs with fewer cores.”.

Also: Microsoft fixes over 1,000 Windows flaws – and one is being exploited.

Two other factors made matters worse, and left servers useless in less than two hours.

In a recent development, “A surge in load increased the likelihood for the networking gateways to encounter the contention,” Lamanna mentioned, explaining that Microsoft 365 maintains two gateway systems. Before the outage started, Teams failed from one to the other, which “changed its traffic patterns.” Simultaneously, he added, “nearly 14% of server capacity for the networking gateway was out of service due to an unrelated concern from the previous day.”.

Those two conditions collided and “caused the network gateway to encounter the latent bug from July,” Lamanna concluded. Requests eventually overloaded servers, at which point they stopped responding. At the outage’s low point, over 80% of its servers weren’t responding.

“When servers lose connectivity, our traffic management systems automatically route users to other healthy endpoints,” Lamanna remarked. “However, the redirected traffic increased the likelihood for the same problem to occur on the remaining endpoints. This caused a cascading failure from server to server as the same amount of load was spread across fewer servers.”.

Also: AI finds zero-day flaws for just $4 now – even mediocre hackers can cash in.

Before Microsoft issued an explanation, some suspected the outage may have been the result of a cyberattack, which both Lamanna and Microsoft’s status account denied.

It’s unclear how many people the outage affected, though Microsoft’s own numbers from January say Microsoft 365 “exceeds 450 million commercial paid seats,” illustrating the scale of the issue. Microsoft deployed an patch to fix the outage and gradually applied it to groups of servers. Lamanna stated Microsoft would publish a full post-incident review with more details later this week.

Sources indicate that service might be restored, but customers aren’t happy about having lost nearly two full workdays. One think tank told CNN it estimated the outage — which lasted through close of business on Friday for some — resulted in $7 billion in losses, due to many businesses and organizations being unable to access their everyday systems.

Also: If the November Windows enhancement fails to install on your PC, here’s what to do.

The fact that Microsoft’s testing couldn’t find the July matter ahead of time may leave customers wondering when the next dormant defect will strike, and whether the tech giant is prepared.

It has been revealed that organizations across Europe have been leaving Microsoft in recent years, opting instead for locally-controlled, open-source alternatives. The former CEO of Github rolled out a decentralized alternative called Entire earlier this year, citing developers’ need for something more reliable, as Github has similarly been plagued with outages.

For many, Teams was barely offline over the two-day period, or was the first service to come back online.

Sources indicate that “Several services like Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint, and Office apps failed out of the faulty network gateway infrastructure. That is why those services were restored earlier, with Teams chats and meetings functioning without glitch for most of the outage,” Lamanna explained. Other services like Exchange Online can’t fail out.

He added that fixing the outage was slow because waiting traffic hit servers as soon as they came back, rendering them unresponsive just as rapidly.

Sources indicate that “Our normally automated recovery processes were not designed to restore service from this broad unresponsive state,” Lamanna stated. “Additionally, since the main code defect was a latent bug from several months previous, our normal rollback, flighting, and feature flags were unable to quickly revert the change.”.

On Thursday morning, people began reporting challenges with Outlook, Teams, and Copilot, according to Downdetector. By 1 p.m. ET, the number of reported Outlook outages was nearly 83,000 but had fallen to just under 75,000 by 2:38 p.m. ET. Teams and Copilot reports started dropping significantly by Thursday evening, but many individuals were still reporting issues accessing systems well into Friday morning on X and Reddit. Even Microsoft’s status page was down until around 3 p.m. ET Thursday.

Also: If the November Windows update fails to install on your PC, here’s what to do.

As late as Friday afternoon, the tech giant didn’t yet have an ETA of when the outage would be fully solved.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • An open-source AI tool designed to find security flaws is helping hackers launch cyberattacks.
  • The advisory was issued the same day communications problems prompted a nationwide Federal Aviation Administration ground stop and a day after a major Microsoft 365 outage began.
  • An FBI official told ABC News⁠ that Artex doesn’t appear to be connected to either incident or to other recent disruptions, including banking outages involving JPMorgan Chase.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An open-source AI tool designed to find security flaws is helping hackers launch cyberattacks. The FBI says hackers are using Artex, an AI-powered security testing tool, to break into organizations worldwide. In an advisory on Friday, the agency said some attacks took less than 3 hours from selecting a target to gaining high-level access to its systems. Attackers have used Artex since at least August against banks, government agencies, technology companies and healthcare providers.

The advisory was issued the same day communications problems prompted a nationwide Federal Aviation Administration ground stop and a day after a major Microsoft 365 outage began. Microsoft attributed its disruption to technical problems, and the FAA states it has found no indication of a cyberattack.

An FBI official told ABC News⁠ that Artex doesn’t appear to be connected to either incident or to other recent disruptions, including banking outages involving JPMorgan Chase.

The warning adds to concerns about the security risks posed by AI agents, which can carry out tasks with little human supervision.

Sources indicate that artex automates security tests that organizations use to uncover weaknesses. According to Microsoft’s analysis, its agents can examine defenses, exploit flaws and extract data. Attackers can use that automation to try several ways into a network simultaneously.

According to recent reports, the FBI cited attacks against South Korean financial institutions that exposed the personal information of approximately 67,000 people. Microsoft warns that attackers breached over 2,250 organizations’ Microsoft 365 systems in a separate campaign, using stolen ConnectWise backup credentials alongside the Artex tool.

Because customers had already authorized the backup software, attackers could use its access without logging in as an individual user. Microsoft cautioned that a successful sign-in doesn’t necessarily mean data was accessed or stolen. The automated attacks could trigger security alerts, but their speed left defenders little time to respond.

This FBI Cyber advisory on ARTEX was released last Friday, 11/13. It is not a new announcement, and the FBI has not issued any additional warning since. The guidance in the advisory remains current.We released this advisory last week because as we head to the end of the year,….

Recent findings suggest that amazon Web Services’ Nov. 13 research described another scheme: Stealing credentials for AI services, and then using that access to hunt for more credentials at someone else’s expense. Amazon Threat Intelligence uncovered the activity through decoy systems posing as AI services. It linked the campaigns to Artex with moderate confidence but couldn’t independently verify results the agents reported on systems outside its monitoring.

Amazon said the attacks relied on default passwords, exposed login details and outdated software, all of which hackers can find and exploit faster with AI.

Industry observers note that artex’s developer removed the original GitHub repository in October after reports of abuse, but copies remain available, the FBI said. The agency recommends limiting access to sensitive systems, reviewing software permissions, replacing exposed credentials, and monitoring unusual account activity or large data transfers.

According to recent reports, even as gas prices dampen some travel plans, you’ll still have plenty of tech giant on the roads this holiday season. AAA predicts that 73 million Americans will travel by car for Thanksgiving between Nov. 24 and Nov. 30. Google Maps is ready to accompany travelers on their journeys with four new features just in time for holiday travel near and far.

In a press release, Google said it’s rolling out four newly introduced Ask Maps features that make it easy to create itineraries, find available appointments, and search your saved lists. Here’s what to know about the latest features coming to Google Maps.

Google has made it easy to build step-by-step itineraries and get real-time route details when you pull up directions. You can use Ask Maps to plan simple tasks, like a day of holiday shopping, or more complex looks, like a multi-day road trip with stops along the way.

According to recent reports, also: I tested Google Maps vs. Waze to find the best navigation app.

You can get a day-by-day schedule with tips and numbered map pins for each stop, which makes it easy to visualize your plan. You can also share your itinerary with friends and family, or export it to Google Docs. It’s like being your own trip planner without outsourcing the work to a travel agent. To access your itinerary, ask Maps to pull it up, or look for the “itinerary” badge in your chat history. This way, you can see real-time details like live traffic conditions, whether a place is open, and more.

Sources indicate that maps can help you stay ahead. You can now pull up directions with helpful tips before you go, tailored to your route and plan. These include tips on where to park or charge your car, as well as real-time updates on conditions such as weather, potential delays, tolls, and more.

We’re heading into the most wonderful (and busiest) time of year for travel and shopping, and Google wants to reduce your stress. Thanks to new agentic capabilities, you can have Ask Maps find beauty, pet care, auto, and home repair appointments online and call local businesses for you. Ask, “Find a 4 p.m. hair appointment near me,” and Ask Maps will show you open slots at nearby businesses so you can book and go. It’s that easy.

If you’re playing host for the holidays, Google will help you show off all your town’s favorite spots. Now you can use Ask Maps to find saved places on your lists. Ask things like, “Which spots saved in my lists have availability for 6 people in the next half-hour?” Ask Maps scans across your lists and checks live availability so you can pick a place and just go.

Also: I’m an Apple Maps fan, but I switch to Google Maps for these 3 tasks.

Recent findings suggest that updates begin rolling out today on Android and iOS, and Ask Maps is also expanding to 30 countries across Europe, including Spain, Germany, and the UK. Ask Maps will now be available in more than 200 countries and territories. Travel itineraries and list search will be available everywhere Ask Maps is offered, while route tips and appointment locating will first launch in the US, with more regions to follow soon, according to Google.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • This includes again accessing end-to-end encrypted messaging without permission, and sharing what may be the bank balances of another Muse user ….

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Meta employees have expressed concerns about what appear to be major privacy breaches when using Muse, right now the second most popular free iPhone app in the App Store with over 10 million downloads.

This includes again accessing end-to-end encrypted messaging without permission, and sharing what may be the bank balances of another Muse user ….

Siri AI was not the only AI app to launch back in September; Meta’s Muse AI app was debuted the same month, with the organization describing it as “your personal AI agent that gets things done across every part of life.”.

Muse initially launched as an iPhone app, with Mac and iPad apps following shortly afterwards. It immediately moved to the top of the US App Store charts, overtaking ChatGPT. It quickly exceeded 5 million downloads following a major advertising push by Meta, and that number has since doubled.

It wasn’t long before major privacy concerns were raised. Tech writer Jason Aten reported that the Mac app accessed his messages despite him explicitly refusing permission. The app then lied to him about how it had achieved this. Meta described this as a bug.

Security researcher Patrick Wardle also discovered a zero-day vulnerability that could allow an attacker to hijack dictated prompts, directing them instead to their own server.

I mentioned at the time that I would absolutely not be one of the millions of people using the app, and the wisdom of that decision has now been underlined by a fresh report.

It has been revealed that reuters now reports Meta employees discussing further breaches. This includes another example of accessing encrypted messages without permission.

An employee using Muse on her personal phone reported it had surprised her with a reminder to respond to a message from her sister on Signal, an end-to-end encrypted messaging service popular with privacy advocates that competes with Meta’s WhatsApp.

It has been revealed that “This seems like an extreme privacy violation. I definitely did not grant it access to other apps, or recall being asked about this,” the employee said in her post.

It has been revealed that the report states this appears to have been done by capturing push notifications. However, this was what the app claimed had happened in the earlier case, and it turned out not to be true. The AI Now Institute was able to replicate the problem of Muse accessing Signal messages without permission.

Another employee reported receiving unsolicited bank balances that they say appeared to be those of another Muse user.

Muse had randomly added an extra message to its regular chats about fishing-related weather and tide information, saying: “BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57.”.

Sources indicate that “I have never shared my bank account with Muse and never discussed any banking topic with Muse. I’m afraid it’s sending other’s bank info to me,” the staffer wrote in his post.

Meta told Reuters that these were “isolated incidents” and suggested that the bank balances may have been AI hallucinations rather than leaked information.

I can only repeat my previous take on Muse: Nope.

#39235. Tech Report: GTA 6 Review: The Megayacht of Gaming Has Something for Nearly Everyone

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 16m • 📚 Deep Dive (3133 w)

Tech Report: GTA 6 Review: The Megayacht of Gaming Has Something for Nearly Everyone

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3133 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The most anticipated game in recent history, Grand Theft Auto 6, lives up to the hype.
  • GTA 6 iterates on the grandness of its predecessor, and in the 13 years since GTA 5 stretched gamer expectations with a huge map of seemingly endless activities, developer Rockstar Games has figured out how to layer a lot of granular detail into its next canvas of crime and carnage.
  • According to recent reports, environments that were sketched out in the last game, such as stores and buildings, are detailed and explorable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The most anticipated game in recent history, Grand Theft Auto 6, lives up to the hype. Expansive, interactive and peppered with so much to do that it’s easy to sink scores of hours into the launch game — and who knows how much more will be added later on.

GTA 6 iterates on the grandness of its predecessor, and in the 13 years since GTA 5 stretched gamer expectations with a huge map of seemingly endless activities, developer Rockstar Games has figured out how to layer a lot of granular detail into its next canvas of crime and carnage.

According to recent reports, environments that were sketched out in the last game, such as stores and buildings, are detailed and explorable. Bystanders and police react more naturally to your presence and culpability — cops now have to see you escaping the crime scene to tag you as a suspect for pursuit. You can talk people down from fights. And the game’s titular transgression of stealing cars is more nuanced than ever.

The standard edition of GTA 6 is available on Amazon now for PS5 and Xbox Series X and S.

If you prefer, you can preorder your copy of GTA 6 from Walmart.

Granted, early versions of some of these advancements were explored in Rockstar’s interim game, 2018’s Red Dead Redemption 2, and the series iteratively progressed with all the updates that continue to this day for GTA Online, which was built out from GTA 5 to be an ever-evolving game-as-a-service. But they’ve been taken to the next level in GTA 6, leading to a world that feels more responsive to your presence and actions. With all its systems, map space and activities, it feels like the megayacht of gaming — a polished experience in all its corners, with some of the most detailed graphics you’ll find in gaming.

A lot of that rests on the shoulders of the game’s protagonists, lovers in crime Lucia and Jason, who operate radically differently from previous GTA point-of-view characters. Their romance (if players choose to pursue it) offers a whole fresh narrative and systematic view of a life outside the law, with collaborative and solo missions that paint a vivid picture of the playful, dangerous world of GTA. Outside story missions, casually driving around as a couple fills the dead air with conversation and the robberies with partnered backup, enriched by their growing relationship, lathering their activities with all the sweetness of a violent date night.

Recent findings suggest that the couple’s story is a very lengthy affair — at 50 hours in, the game says I’ve completed roughly 70% of it — and is robust enough to justify the price of entry. It’s a compelling narrative about two people trying to build a future through a dangerous world by leaning deeper into the danger, but it’s also a showcase of the world Rockstar built. After the story is done, the game hands you the keys to explore it yourself however you’d like.

In a recent development, rockstar declined to comment on whether GTA 6 will transition into the next version of GTA Online, but it feels like an inevitability. It’s hard to ignore the vast space, systems and mechanics that players only briefly dabble with while playing through the story. From fishing to treasure hunting in underwater shipwrecks to major game hunting to street racing, there’s a lot of low-stakes fodder to unwind with the game — and plenty of bank heists, chases and other random crimes to ratchet up the tension, too.

In a recent development, at launch, GTA 6 has a broad foundation of things to do that — I suspect — will increase over time. It’s layered with Rockstar’s signature puerile humor, and I’ll fess up to laughing at some of the frequent boner jokes and crass names (one sportscar brand is the “pfister”), but the occasional homophobia and transphobia is bizarrely out of time — the game’s mock-everything culture still feels rooted in the 2000s, aimed at people who loved the edginess of South Park in its heyday. More modern satire appears in bystander conversations that range into absurd caricatures of far-right anti-woke crusaders and rabid leftists, but given the game’s faux-Florida setting in the fictional state of Leonida (which includes the legendary Vice City), there’s far more of the former than the latter.

Sources indicate that thus, the world feels textured even for players just picking up the game to fool around. While there are sparse stretches of the map, little side stories unfold for those who notice and follow strange things afoot. But a massive part of the game’s appeal and heart lies in the ballad of two lovebirds, kept apart by immaturity and circumstance but brought together through crime and the skewed American dream at the center of every GTA: Pull off a substantial enough heist and the world is yours.

The game’s story opens from Jason’s perspective — a twentysomething guy, former military, quiet and gruff, drifting through life doing odd jobs for a small-time kingpin out in the sticks. A little drug-running and skirmishing with the local gangs keep him busy, working out and drinking beers on his deck, watching the sunset from GTA 6’s version of the Florida Keys.

Sources indicate that all that changes when Lucia, who stole and then broke his heart, gets out of prison on early release and asks to crash with him during her parole. A tenuous second chance is complicated when she reconnects with a former cellmate who’s partnered with a rich hotshot dangling wealth in front of our fragile couple. This could be the ticket to a financial foundation to help them start anew. Then a job goes wrong, and the pair go on the run, restarting in a rural backwater as far from the clubs of Vice City as one can get.

Recent findings suggest that this is where players decide how close they want Jason and Lucia to be. The game sets up the beginnings of their reconnection, but they can drift apart if players don’t choose to bring them closer. It’s all about the little things: Jason holding the door for Lucia, one of them buying clothes for the other at the vendor, or even just sidling close during morning coffee. Rockstar didn’t want to force players into this relationship — even if things fizzle, the pair will still go through the game as partners in crime, doing jobs together even if they sleep apart.

Industry observers note that but players will value something if they have to work for it, Rob Nelson, head of development at Rockstar North, told me over a video call. He likened the couple’s relationship to how players embraced the honor system in RDR2, with more taking the high honor route than being a vicious criminal.

“When you can lose something, it’s more meaningful if you work to keep it,” Nelson noted.

As Nelson explained, Rockstar came off of GTA 5’s story with its three protagonists wondering how to one-up it for the sequel, which started development soon after in 2015 but took until early 2019 to settle on GTA 6’s main pair. A romantic couple is indeed a step up from characters who come together for a job and split after, and Rockstar had to figure out how that’s different for lovers — they’re not going to end a job at 2 a.m. and part ways; they’re going home to go to bed, Nelson mentioned.

According to recent reports, the couple essentially have a run-on conversation that lasts through the story, piping up during long drives to chat about a recent mission or bring up something from their pasts. How much these topics are tailored to events and how much are randomly chosen feels cleverly obscured, coming off like the natural chatter between two people slowly figuring each other out. The sheer scale of the recorded dialogue dwarfs other games and becomes a feature among many, showcasing the titanic work Rockstar put into GTA 6.

It has been revealed that it all adds up to a compelling narrative centered on two characters, carefully chiseled to embody the best and worst of Vice City, inspired by the real-life Bonnie and Clyde and by crime couples from films like True Romance and Natural Born Killers. GTA 6’s couple starts with a meet-cute over trying to steal the same car, and freshly out of prison, Lucia eggs on Jason to take bigger illegal jobs than the small-time gigs he’s coasted on. Even with an ankle monitor and picking up road trash on work duty, Lucia never seriously considers staying on the right side of the law. Jason is cautious about latest opportunities, but eager not to lose Lucia again, and never considers going straight.

Recent findings suggest that nestled within their stories is a serious point about the futility of staying honest in a city and system that caters to the rich and punishes the desperate. A flashback reveals Lucia juggling gig-economy rideshare driving and having her utilities shut off after failed payments, which is heartbreakingly real. But it’s a blip amid the overwhelming focus on a criminal romance, where the only escape from poverty is to steal big bills until finally retiring to a distant island beyond the consequences of your felonious lifestyle.

It’s not surprising — that’s the GTA fantasy, after all — but it’s telling which things Rockstar took great pains to upgrade to modern tastes over the game’s decade-plus development (and what it left out). Smartphones are a huge part of the game’s social interactions, from texting and calling contacts to Instagram-like social media feeds to summoning cars through an app or hailing a ride. But notably absent are any gig economy services that have normalized atypical incomes — you can’t TaskRabbit or Uber your way to an honest living in GTA 6. Odd jobs come as under-the-table favors you do for the rich and powerful, frequently taking advantage of both protagonists’ gray morals.

Sources indicate that though it won’t give you the option of a legal living, GTA 6 leans into the injustice of the wealth gap, putting a few city blocks between gang-riddled run-down apartments and the high-rise clubs populated by ignorant rich assholes. The game gleefully showcases the hypocrisy of the privileged — one time, I rushed into a rural, well-off house where a wife espousing family values ushered me to help her dying husband… who was choking in a BDSM leather harness. Once freed, he tucked his tail back into his submissive role as a “liberal cuck” for their roleplay.

This kind of edginess-for-laughs is peppered around the game, and it’s hard not to feel the cynicism. I can de-escalate some situations, but a lot of the non-player characters you run into on the street are on a hair-trigger, eager to fight. You’ll overhear plenty of anti-immigrant screeds from random bystanders. Junkies try to break into your car if you have contraband in the trunk.

Industry observers note that if GTA 5 was released in the waning Obama years with waning public optimism, GTA 6 introduces halfway into Trump’s second term, where far-right government ICE deportations and street killings have polarized the nation beyond anything we’ve seen in decades. Yet when I asked how Rockstar had adjusted the game over its long development to suit this moment, Nelson said that Jason and Lucia’s story is a counterweight of optimism and care amid all the crime and societal disparity in the game.

It has been revealed that “Choosing love is a bit of an act of rebellion against a narcissistic culture,” Nelson mentioned. “The ideas of selfishness and selflessness put through this world is interesting to us, giving you goals other than just maxing out your bank account with supercars and properties.”.

In a recent development, evaluating a game with so much detail spread across a vast map area is difficult, as the polish can be mistaken for quality. When I parked in a narrow driveway, I noticed Jason has an entire animation for shimmying through a slim gap. There have to be a dozen sequences for ways he and Lucia can sidle up to each other for a quick peck or embrace, all optional. There must be a thousand or more buildings you can duck into to explore their interiors. And the amount of dialogue feels unfathomably colossal, all voiced with aplomb by talented actors.

It has been revealed that where other games have some, GTA 6 has more. It’s a little like asking whether a megayacht is enjoyable to commute to work. The simple answer is yes, GTA 6 is an incredible game. And yet, its scope can be distracting. Halfway through the story, I was zipping from destroying drug dens to stealing valuable cars for a collector to hunting major game in the rural hills — all good fun, but my attention easily peeled away from the main story and the couple’s attempt to secure their financial independence, retire early future. The prior chapter had ended in a gun battle as hired killers came for a dangerous MacGuffin in Jason and Lucia’s hands, but amid all the good, clean street crime, that danger had receded to the background.

According to recent reports, the story’s punch is diluted by everything you can and probably will do, which feels like forgetting the taste of the prime rib after sampling everything else at a buffet. But at least all those activities are enjoyable and round out the criminal with the casual, including mini golf and mud races far from the dense urban core of Vice City. It’s like if Lego Island grew up to add larceny to its roster of fun things to do.

In grappling with the scale of the game, I repeatedly reach for simile — too many options make it harder to fully define GTA 6 and who it’s for, outside of saying there’s so much that its appeal spreads very wide. There’s not quite something for everyone, but it offers such a plethora of side activities that if one gets tiring, another will probably tide you over. This is what will most likely form the foundation of an eventual transition to GTA Online: A substantial stream of things to do on top of stacking cash. And given GTAO’s sustained success, the baseline version of GTA 6 will please all the heist junkies and freeform adventurers who’ve loved the series, even if they aren’t hooked by the well-crafted core story. All the looky-loos curious about the hype will find one of the most polished and visually gorgeous video games ever made.

Recent findings suggest that GTA fans will notice a lot of small improvements that clean up logical inconsistencies. Witnesses have to notice you doing a crime to report it, and cops have to see you flee a crime scene to put out an all-points bulletin on your description, though you can lower your chances of being recognized by swapping outfits and respraying the color of your getaway ride.

Other new features add complexity to the game. Certain crimes are riskier until you get new tools and connections unlocked through the story, which let you steal cars with trackers and rob banks with countermeasures. Exercise and diet affect your health and physique, which you’ll need to maintain with regular workouts. You can steal guns and vehicles, but they won’t be saved unless you pay to buy or register them, respectively.

These sound tedious, but they’re little frictions that make living in the world of GTA 6 more intentional. Early in the game as Jason, I frequently found myself waking up in the morning, grabbing a cup of coffee and doing a workout to get my in-game day “started,” putting on the radio and feeding my snake or checking in with Lucia ambling around the kitchen. As the relationship between the two deepens, they can go to bed together, cuddled up and doomscrolling on their phones.

In a recent development, while I expect a million posts of “he just like me fr fr” to blanket social media as people wonder at the work Rockstar put in to replicate our (often terrible) habits, there’s still a lot I was delighted to discover that’s unique to the world they’ve made. Some of these are jokes taken to an extreme, like the intentionally pretentious game-within-a-game you can play, Tenebrae Lux — a black-and-white walking simulator by an in-universe auteur, Johannes Zuch, whose name flashes on the screen so many times that it feels like a wink toward Hideo Kojima and other famous game creators.

“We love auteurs — it’s not mocking, it’s celebrating,” Nelson said.

But my favorite things in any GTA game are the side stories you can chance upon that are scripted but feel emergent, exploring the bizarre nooks and crannies of the world. One night halfway through the game, I was casually driving around as Lucia when I saw a police chopper aiming a spotlight at the street — and found the cops in a standoff with a man in a fox suit.

In a recent development, I immediately discovered that, in the game’s fictional state of Leonida, being a furry (e.g., wearing a fur suit and expressing your “fursona”) is illegal, so I broke through the police blockade to liberate him. I met up with his fellow furries and spirited them away to a compound, during which I peeked over my shoulder to find them nuzzling each other. God bless you little oddballs bravely living your truth in the face of unjust laws.

Industry observers note that like its forebears, GTA 6 feels like two games — a core narrative about making a living through the underground in a rags-to-riches-to-rags-to-riches saga of a star-crossed couple, and a massive sandbox to do whatever you want. While going treasure hunting in offshore wrecks or making drug drop-offs from a plane dilutes the story’s tension, it also gives you a lot of opportunity to find the GTA you want to experience. After the story fades into memory, that’s what’ll stick around as the core of this game: the freedom to choose what you want to do, laws be damned.

Eventually, you’ll face that ultimate temptation to cause such havoc that you’ll trigger the game’s upcoming, sixth star of police attention — one in which it feels like every cop in Leonida is coming after you, and it doesn’t stop until you’re arrested or put down, a countdown to how long Jason and Lucia can stick it to the law at maximum volume.

“I haven’t played six stars since we finalized it. I made it too long, so we made it harder,” Nelson remarked. “I’m curious to see what times people get!”.

  • A stock split allows a publicly traded manufacturer to alter its share price and outstanding share count by the same factor without affecting its market cap or underlying operating performance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sean Williams – Nov 19, 2026 at 5:06AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Sandisk ›.

Though the last four years have been dominated by the evolution of artificial intelligence (AI), AI isn't the only trend propelling the stock market to latest heights. Stock-split euphoria has also played an important role -- and later today, Nov. 19, these two catalysts will converge.

After the close of trading today, Wall Street's next blockbuster stock split becomes effective, with memory and storage solutions specialist Sandisk (SNDK +6.54%), which is up nearly 2,400% since its February 2025 debut, completing its first-ever split.

A stock split allows a publicly traded manufacturer to alter its share price and outstanding share count by the same factor without affecting its market cap or underlying operating performance. Though there are two varieties of splits, investors tend to gravitate toward one and shy away from the other.

Sources indicate that reverse stock splits, designed to increase a organization's share price, are often shunned by investors. This type of split is typically undertaken by struggling companies attempting to avoid delisting from a major stock exchange.

Sources indicate that by comparison, investors tend to pile into companies announcing and completing forward stock splits. Forward splits make a firm's stock more nominally affordable for everyday investors who can't purchase fractional shares through their broker.

NASDAQ · As of 9:44 AM ET 11/19/26.

More importantly, companies enacting forward splits are usually firing on all cylinders, with consistent sales and profit growth. If a public firm needs to lower its share price to ensure retail investors can take part in its growth story, it must be doing something right.

After the close of trading today, Sandisk will effect an 8-for-1 forward split, reducing its share price to (presumably) a little over $100 and increasing its outstanding share count by a factor of eight.

It has been revealed that businesses are spending nothing short of an arm and a leg on the AI infrastructure build-out, and Sandisk has been one of the prime beneficiaries. The company's NAND flash memory solutions and solid-state drives are being gobbled up in bulk.

The AI data center expansion is benefiting Sandisk on both ends. The insatiable demand for its memory and storage solutions, coupled with ongoing supply shortages for AI hardware, has collectively beefed up its pricing power and lifted its gross margin to never-before-seen levels. Sandisk's gross margin reached 85% in the fiscal first quarter (ending Oct. 2) on $11.03 billion in sales.

Currently, Galaxy AI lives inside your Galaxy devices and apps, but its smarts are limited to the apps it’s integrated with. It has been revealed that with a more agentic assistant, it can access Mom’s contact card and her birthdate, calculate two days before her birthday, and remind you on that date. Like Gemini Intelligence and Siri AI, Personal Agent Core will need special permissions to access your sensitive information, such as messages, photos, and calls.

Also: 4 ways Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.

Also: I’m a ChatGPT power user, but I won’t give it my wallet.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, in light of growing pushback from owners who want more control over how AI is integrated into their apps (if at all), Canva is introducing new settings that let them hide generative AI features and see less AI-generated content.
  • Canva today revealed new controls that will let Free and Pro users choose whether to see generative AI features across the app, as well as how much AI-generated content appears in search results and in recommendations for templates and design elements.
  • The company notes that both controls are available at no additional cost and can be turned on or off at any time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in light of growing pushback from owners who want more control over how AI is integrated into their apps (if at all), Canva is introducing new settings that let them hide generative AI features and see less AI-generated content. Here are the details.

Canva today revealed new controls that will let Free and Pro users choose whether to see generative AI features across the app, as well as how much AI-generated content appears in search results and in recommendations for templates and design elements.

The company notes that both controls are available at no additional cost and can be turned on or off at any time.

According to Canva, “the future of creativity isn’t a choice between AI and no AI.” For this reason, it is introducing the following controls:.

The company indicates that, while it knows that there is an ongoing debate between owners with opposing views on whether AI has a place in creative work, it thinks “both views are valid”:.

“It’s not our place to tell anyone how to create, so today we’re launching two newly introduced controls that put that decision firmly with our community […].”.

Importantly, the tech giant noted that select features that use AI without generating newly introduced content will remain available even when generative AI features are turned off:.

Industry observers note that “Some of Canva’s everyday editing tools use AI to make simple tasks faster, without generating anything new. Background Remover, one of Canva’s most popular tools, lifts a subject cleanly out of a photo in a single click, and Magic Grab lets creators select an object in an image and move it somewhere else in the design. Both remain available when the generative AI switch is off, because they work only with what’s already in a design.”.

Canva added that these tools also won’t add an AI label to a design’s metadata, since that label is reserved for AI-generated content.

As for the company’s design content library, Canva mentioned that while “a small portion of the library is AI-generated content made by Canva, including some abstract backgrounds and illustrated graphics,” its community has told it “they want an easier way to find design assets made by real people, so the content control reduces the number of AI-generated templates and elements that appear in search results and recommendations.”.

With today’s announcement, Canva is essentially expanding on the AI permissions already available to administrators of Business, Enterprise, Teams, and Education accounts, which let organizations control how their teams use AI.

Canva’s official announcement should go live here shortly, and we’ll enhancement this post with the direct link once it’s up.

#39230. How the European Commission rolled out Matrix to more than 40k staff

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Element ↗ Open Full Page

How the European Commission rolled out Matrix to more than 40k staff

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1106 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Element

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the European Commission went from a Matrix proof of concept in December 2025 to a sovereign communication tool rolled out to every Commission laptop by September 2026.
  • At The Matrix Conference 2026, Diana Gheorghe, Head of Sector for Digital Workplace Communication and Collaboration Services, and Alexandru Vignide, Service Delivery Manager for the Commission's sovereign communication tool, told the story of how they got there.
  • “Sovereignty” can have a different meaning for different people and organisations, so the Commission started by pinning down what it means for them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the European Commission went from a Matrix proof of concept in December 2025 to a sovereign communication tool rolled out to every Commission laptop by September 2026. That tool, built on Matrix by Element, and run by the Commission itself, now serves more than 40,000 owners.

At The Matrix Conference 2026, Diana Gheorghe, Head of Sector for Digital Workplace Communication and Collaboration Services, and Alexandru Vignide, Service Delivery Manager for the Commission's sovereign communication tool, told the story of how they got there. The pair were transparent about what got harder at scale, and how they dealt with it.

“Sovereignty” can have a different meaning for different people and organisations, so the Commission started by pinning down what it means for them. Their answer spans five dimensions: resilience and business continuity, vendor diversity, control over their data, ownership of the platform, and leverage in procurement - the ability to negotiate with, or walk away from, a supplier. That last one is easy to forget, and arguably the one that bites hardest when it's missing.

In a recent development, for internal communications specifically, the priorities were resilience, data ownership and, crucially, interoperability. That's what led them to Matrix: an open protocol whose value lies in letting separate systems talk to each other. They chose Element Server Suite Pro (ESS Pro), Element's enterprise distribution of Matrix, as a mature implementation, and decided to host, operate and architect the service under their own control.

With the building blocks chosen, Alexandru walked through three architecture decisions.

Industry observers note that hosting. The service doesn't run in a Commission-owned data centre. Instead it runs with sovereign cloud providers selected through the sovereign hosting tender awarded earlier this year, in order to meet its sovereignty and hosting requirements. Sovereign doesn't have to mean building everything in-house; it means choosing who you depend on, and on what terms.

According to recent reports, identity. The deployment is integrated with EU Login, the sign-in staff already use every day. A new tool is easier to adopt when logging in feels familiar.

Federation. Connecting to Matrix servers outside the Commission is still under assessment. The technical side is being explored - there was a separate hands-on demo using non-production environments at the conference - but federation also needs governance, participation and structure, which takes longer to agree than a config change.

The Commission started working with Matrix in summer 2025, or, as Alexandru put it, at last year's Matrix Conference. From there, things moved quickly:.

The Commission is now exploring a mobile rollout, and what federation could look like.

Industry observers note that rolling out to 40,000 people surfaces problems no pilot will. Alexandru described the four main ones his team ran into, and how they tackled each.

Finding colleagues across servers. The Commission runs several Synapse homeservers, and early on, people on different servers couldn't always find each other. The Commission's teams worked with Element to fix this, and now a plain user search finds anyone in the Commission, whichever server they're on.

Accounts that only appear after sign-up. The Commission chose user-led account creation rather than pre-provisioning every account. The catch is that you can't find a colleague who hasn't registered yet, which made the discovery problem above feel worse while adoption was still ramping up.

Recent findings suggest that live presence was switched off. As more consumers came on board, the load from live presence (the real-time “online/away” indicator) started to affect performance, so the team disabled it. They're now looking at a user status feature being developed with Element as the replacement.

Recent findings suggest that infrastructure had to learn to scale itself. Rolling out in waves over three months meant uneven, shifting demand, so the team tuned the infrastructure to adjust automatically.

In a recent development, running through all of this was the balance between security and usability. Most of the hardening work was done with the Commission's security teams before the rollout, and continues through regular security reviews and continuous improvements. The team made sure that hardening didn't get in the way of everyday tasks like creating an account, recovering it or verifying a newly introduced device, and documented those steps clearly for staff. Feedback from tickets, internal forums and public channels is consolidated into prioritised goals for the Commission's own roadmap.

It has been revealed that the most common question, Diana noted, is whether Element is meant to replace Microsoft Teams, or consumer apps like Signal and WhatsApp. The short answer: neither, directly. Element is positioned as an internal communication tool for specific use cases - secure communication among them - where the Commission's existing stack doesn't fully meet its needs. Teams bundles communication, collaboration and a whole platform behind it, so there's no one-to-one swap to be had.

According to recent reports, that makes expectation-setting part of the job. People naturally compare workplace tools with the apps they use at home and go looking for feature-for-feature matches. Diana's view is that this mindset is something to address head-on in any organisational change: Element is a tool in its own right, with its own feature set, that the Commission and Element can evolve together.

Part of the goal is to bring work conversations onto a tool the Commission controls.

In a recent development, the Commission has been interested in federation for a long time. The obvious starting point is other EU institutions, but it wouldn't stop there: the Commission also works closely with member states, governments and non-governmental organisations.

It has been revealed that no decision has been made yet, and the Commission is taking it one step at a time. First comes the technical question of what the technology can actually do, because, as Diana put it, there's no point writing policies technology can't deliver. Then comes governance: who the partners would be, on what terms, with what scope, and how security and privacy are handled.

Alexandru ended the talk by sharing what the deployment had taught the Commission.

Sovereignty is operational. It depends on operational control and the trustworthiness of the whole chain of partners, not just on where the service is hosted.

Adoption depends on everyday usability. Discoverability, onboarding support and everything around the product shape whether people use it.

In a recent development, interoperability needs more than technology. It also needs clear structure, participation and governance.

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, disney is celebrating 75 years of its Imagineers, who have been amusing and delighting guests with audio-animatronic characters since talking parrots debuted in the Enchanted Tiki Room at Disneyland.
  • In partnership with Amazon Web Services, AI has helped Walt Disney Imagineering create three new Anzellan animatronics that will live bring a Disney theme park retail space to life, presumably in Star Wars: Galaxy’s Edge.
  • Industry observers note that anzellans are a race of tiny humanoid creatures that repair droids and starships in the Star Wars universe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, disney is celebrating 75 years of its Imagineers, who have been amusing and delighting guests with audio-animatronic characters since talking parrots debuted in the Enchanted Tiki Room at Disneyland. But today, newly introduced robotic characters are being powered up with artificial intelligence.

In partnership with Amazon Web Services, AI has helped Walt Disney Imagineering create three new Anzellan animatronics that will live bring a Disney theme park retail space to life, presumably in Star Wars: Galaxy’s Edge.

Industry observers note that anzellans are a race of tiny humanoid creatures that repair droids and starships in the Star Wars universe. They include Babu Frik in Star Wars: Episode IX — The Rise of Skywalker and the droidsmiths introduced in season 3 of The Mandalorian. The droidsmiths take on larger roles in The Mandalorian and Grogu, helping Baby Yoda rescue Din Djarin from the Hutts.

The fresh Anzellan animatronics built by Disney Imagineers use AWS cloud and AI capabilities in order to “understand the scene around them,” Kyle Laughlin, SVP of Walt Disney Imagineering R&D and Technology and Engineering, tells me.

“If you imagine walking into an experiential retail store, you now will be greeted not by a pre-scripted animation or interaction, but a totally personalized experience where each of these Anzellans [has] their own personalities,” Laughlin says, adding that they’ll be attuned to how many people are nearby and whether they’re children or adults.

The animatronic aliens will be able to interact with guests, right down to commenting on people who are wearing a birthday button or even a certain Star Wars T-shirt. Speaking with these animatronics will give guests the same experience they would have when meeting a character walking around the park, Laughlin adds. They also play off each other and react to what each other are doing, with no one controlling them behind the scenes.

It has been revealed that the three audio-animatronic prototypes, which will make their first appearance during AWS re:Invent in Las Vegas on Nov. 30 before moving into one of the Disney Parks, are named Vilo Vele, Kado Bre’a and Jibu Bre’a.

They’re original characters created just for this project in partnership with Lucasfilm and the filmmakers, and they all have their own personalities devised by the Imagineers. Vilo is the boss, Kado is the droidsmith mechanic who wants to be the center of attention and Jibu, though Kado’s twin, is the shy one. The animatronics speak a mix of English (or Galactic Basic in-universe) and Anzellan, as they do in the Star Wars movies and TV series, and have hundreds of thousands of prerecorded lines of dialogue to draw from when talking to guests and each other.

Samira Panah Bakhtiar, AWS general manager of Telco, Media & Entertainment, Games, Advertising and Sports, tells me this is “one of the most delightful examples” of physical AI.

Industry observers note that “When you talk about physical AI, it’s AI that perceives, it reasons and it acts in the real world,” she says. “It’s not just AI on a screen.”.

Bakhtiar notes Disney was able to use both AWS cloud computing and AI tools to “get from idea to implementation several magnitudes faster than they would have otherwise,” with Laughlin specifying it took “mere months.”.

According to recent reports, AWS staff used a coding agent called Kiro that built their creative briefs into software, which was then reviewed and approved by humans. Imagineers also used the Amazon Bedrock fully managed AI service, which allows them to choose between all the biggest AI models, including those from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta.

“We’re providing Amazon Bedrock to the Imagineering team to be able to leverage the right models that they need at the right time to be able to really enhance those character experiences,” Bakhtiar tells me. “From multimodal models that focus on voice to world models, to large language models. The point is that they are able to get the right tool at the right time and then do so in a way that’s secure, resilient, performant and globally available.”.

Bakhtiar says AWS is continuing to work with Disney, though the next project is under wraps.

“The future of entertainment is going to be highly personalized,” she notes. “It’s going to be multidimensional, and it’s going to be more interactive than ever. And I think this is an incredible example of that coming to life.”.

Disney had previously teamed up with Nvidia on robotics and AI to bring a robot version of fan-favorite Frozen character Olaf to life so he can wander around Disneyland Paris and Hong Kong Disneyland, and is also now exploring robots paired with AI that could guide guests throughout Disneyland parking lots.

“You can imagine an entire franchise of characters working and interacting with one another,” claims Laughlin. “We’ve done a number of things in the Star Wars universe. We’re just getting started in Frozen, and we have a wealth of IP that we can mine to bring those characters to our guests as fast as possible.”.

Sources indicate that correction, 3:48 p.m. ET: The original version of this story incorrectly stated who used the Kiro coding agent to build the software. It was staff from AWS.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Although the iPhone Duo was released just this fall, Apple is finalizing the foldable’s second generation. According to a Bloomberg report, Apple has already created prototypes for the second iPhone Duo, codenamed V78, and some include a sought-after feature: Face ID.

Apple reportedly wants to bring Face ID to the foldable, potentially integrating it into the outer display. However, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman notes that Apple appears to be running out of time to finalize its plans for the Duo ahead of a fall 2027 launch.

Also: iPhone Duo review: Hard to recommend, even harder to put down.

Industry observers note that iPhone launch events typically take place in early September, when Apple releases its newly introduced smartphone lineups. To have the iPhones ready for sale on the heels of their announcement, Apple must manufacture the new models well before the launch event.

Because of this timeline concern, Face ID isn’t guaranteed for the iPhone Duo 2, though it could come to a third generation instead.

Other planned uogrades — including an Action Button, a telephoto camera, and a thinner, lighter construction — are also noted in the report.

Apple reportedly wants to add an Action Button, the customizable button that performs an action when pressed. The iPhone Duo 2 may combine the Action Button and the Camera Control buttons into a single button, providing a useful physical shortcut instead of adding a new button.

The report indicates that many users don’t use the camera control button as often as Apple expected. Combining the camera and action buttons gives Apple the real estate necessary to add both options in an already constrained space.

According to recent reports, apple also wants to incorporate a telephoto camera into the iPhone Duo, though this is likely to happen in one of the next couple of generations. A telephoto camera would give customers greater flexibility to zoom in and capture clear photos of distant objects, which would be an upgrade to the Duo’s photography features.

Technically, equipping the Duo with a telephoto camera is feasible, but the biggest obstacle is space constraints. A telephoto camera needs more room than a wide-angle one, since it requires additional optical elements to magnify distant objects.

Apple already uses a tetraprism design in its Pro iPhones, which allows a longer optical path without too much physical depth.

Apple also wants to reduce the weight and thickness of the iPhone Duo, which is legitimately clunky and cumbersome. To do this, Apple needs to balance the large internal and outer displays, battery capacity, camera array, and the hinge mechanism.

Also: The iPhone Action Button you’re hardly using has a superpower.

For many consumers, reducing the weight and thickness of a passport-sized foldable could matter more in buying decisions than adding another button or camera.

According to recent reports, gurman’s latest report doesn’t mention any planned changes for the iPhone Duo’s hinge mechanism, even after concerns with the first generation’s durability. With manufacturing deadlines fast approaching, however, it’s unlikely that Apple will be able to make changes to the Duo 2 based on consumer feedback. More than likely, these changes would come with the third-generation model.

In a recent development, CNET tested the iPhone Duo’s hinge mechanism and found that, after around 440,000 cycles, the hinge stopped opening flat on its own. Loosening and other signs of wear were evident after 390,000 folds.

Also: The best iPhone Duo cases: Expert recommended.

Given the thinner, lighter construction of a future Duo model, one could assume that changes to the hinge and the foldable’s internal structure are imminent, but this has not been confirmed.

Sources indicate that because Apple will not have enough time to gather feedback on the iPhone Duo before the manufacturing deadlines for the iPhone Duo 2, I don’t expect the second-generation iPhone Duo to be significantly different from its predecessor. We do expect a thinner iPhone Duo 2 and a way to incorporate the Action and Camera buttons.

Which Laptops Last the Longest? Check Out the Laptops I’ve Tested With the Best Battery Life

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (649 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I can almost guarantee that your next laptop will run longer on battery power than whatever you’re right now using.
  • With many of today’s laptops, you can leave the charger at home for days at a time.
  • This increase in battery life is one of the biggest stories in laptops this year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I can almost guarantee that your next laptop will run longer on battery power than whatever you’re right now using. We’ve seen a huge leap in laptop battery life in recent years, to the point where getting 20 or more hours on a single charge isn’t uncommon. This year alone, the average battery life of the laptops we’ve tested at CNET has increased by more than five hours. And it’s nearly doubled since the start of the decade.

With many of today’s laptops, you can leave the charger at home for days at a time. The longest-lasting laptop I tested this year lasted more than 34 hours!

This increase in battery life is one of the biggest stories in laptops this year. In the laptop episode of our video series Holiday Office Hours From the Labs, I explain what’s behind this surge in battery life and highlight some of the laptops that lasted the longest in testing.

Plus, my colleagues Kyle Kucharski from ZDNET and Joe Osborne from PCMag share their own holiday laptop picks. Kyle looks at Apple’s entry-level MacBook Neo and its imitators, and Joe breaks down what to look for in a budget gaming laptop.

Recent findings suggest that unlike raw performance, where the more you spend, the more you get, lengthy battery life can be found just as easily in a budget laptop as in an expensive, high-end powerhouse. And, in fact, less powerful components and lower screen resolutions can give cheaper laptops an edge in battery life.

According to recent reports, the biggest factor behind longer battery life in laptops is the advancement in mobile processors. They’ve become much more power efficient, and in the case of Apple’s and Qualcomm’s chips, they’re based on an architecture other than the traditional x86 instruction set that’s been at the heart of Intel processors since the dawn of the PC era.

Apple’s run of battery-life winners started when it shifted from Intel processors to its own M-series chips. Apple’s M-series processors are based on the Arm architecture, a power-efficient chip architecture found in phones and tablets. Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X-series processors are also Arm-based, and they can be found in the two longest-running laptops we’ve tested: the HP OmniBook 3 16 and OmniBook 5 14. The OmniBook 3 16’s record-setting battery performance earned it a CNET Lab Award for longest battery life.

In a recent development, intel has made huge strides in processor efficiency with its last two generations of chips: the Core Ultra 200 series developed under the name Lunar Lake, and the Core Ultra 300 series, also known as Panther Lake. Last year, the Lenovo Yoga 9i 2-in-1 Aura Edition became the first Intel laptop to last longer than a day, running for 25 hours, 45 minutes in testing. It’s still the longest-running Intel laptop we’ve tested, but the MSI Prestige 14 Flip AI Plus with Intel’s next-gen Core Ultra X7 358H processor came close with a time of 25 hours, 18 minutes.

Read more: Laptops With the Best Battery Life.

Recent findings suggest that whether Arm or x86, there are two more reasons behind greater processor efficiency and longer laptop battery life. For one, the size of a processor shrinks with every generation. The smaller a processor is and the more tightly packed its components are, the less power is required to flip its tinier transistors on and off. For another, today’s mobile processors feature more flexible designs with a mix of performance and efficiency cores. A processor engages its higher-performance cores only when needed, using the efficiency cores for as many general, everyday tasks as possible, so your laptop stays cool and quiet and runs longer.

For more, you can read my Labs exclusive on the huge increase in laptop battery life this year and check out the video above for my holiday laptop picks and those from my colleagues.
