#39225. 5 ways AI will change how you defend your business in 2027

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1173 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Zdnet ↗ Open Full Page

5 ways AI will change how you defend your business in 2027

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1173 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • At the beginning of the year, few organizations were utilizing large language models (LLMs) and AI agents in their cybersecurity workflows, including for discovering and patching vulnerabilities.
  • Also: Rogue AI incidents hit ‘tens of thousands’: Can businesses trust these tools?
  • The capabilities of agentic AI are fast outstripping the speed and scale at which traditional security operations centers (SOCs) can operate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At the beginning of the year, few organizations were utilizing large language models (LLMs) and AI agents in their cybersecurity workflows, including for discovering and patching vulnerabilities. According to Google, this is now happening at scale.

Also: Rogue AI incidents hit ‘tens of thousands’: Can businesses trust these tools?

The capabilities of agentic AI are fast outstripping the speed and scale at which traditional security operations centers (SOCs) can operate. Like it or not, AI has an integral role in the latest reality — for the defenders and threat actors.

According to recent reports, speed and scale are the main reasons enterprises consider adopting AI in SOCs and for security more broadly, and these factors underpin Google’s new security forecast for 2027 — Cloud CISO Perspectives. However, without the right precautions, AI security adopters could inadvertently increase their attack surface rather than shrink it.

With this in mind, these are five ways AI will change the security industry over the next year and what CISOs need to consider going into 2027.

Alert fatigue is well-known across SOC teams. Alert after alert needs to be trawled through; many are irrelevant or false positives, tying up skilled staff with the mundane, tedious, time-consuming task of triaging them.

Now that autonomous, AI-driven threats can probe a network, gain entry, and move laterally across it in minutes, chasing threat data and security alerts from multiple systems logged days or weeks ago can’t help a business mitigate them — and certainly not at the speed of the threat.

According to Google’s forecast, AI will mean the alert queue quietly disappears. Ramya Chitrakar, VP of engineering at Google Cloud Security, believes that “2027 is the year analysts stop chasing alerts and start shaping outcomes.”.

Also: AI is both a cyber weapon and a massive target.

How? CISOs must change the alert model itself. Instead of human defenders triaging alerts at the start of a cybersecurity incident, the alert becomes final output, with autonomous agents handling “data enrichment, correlation, and triage automatically, surfacing a verified conclusion rather than a raw ticket,” according to Google.

This means cybersecurity experts can oversee alert handling and verify automated actions, potentially freeing them to focus on other tasks.

Industry observers note that custom agentic AI is often designed — or at least intended — to work autonomously, with human oversight. However, having thousands of individual agents working across multiple environments can create high-value entry points into corporate networks that cyberattackers target.

We need to think of agentic AI as more than a tool: each one needs its own identity, like a human employee, to operate within a zero-trust architecture, retain control, and reduce the risk of compromise.

Also: Your enterprise AI access can be sold for pennies – beware ‘LLM Mixers’.

According to recent reports, however, Heather Adkins, VP of security engineering at Google, thinks this needs to go further and suggests the zero-trust concept shouldn’t stop at the network layer. Instead, Adkins believes it needs to reach the transaction layer.

A paper trail for each agent needs to be established, which is impossible to handle manually, and even within a zero-trust framework, AI agents could be given too much scope. Instead, implement verification for each transaction and for every authorization, and assign each AI agent its own least-privilege set of credentials that can be revoked if there is a security incident or the agent is no longer required.

“When backed by real-time autonomous reasoning, we can dynamically allow a transaction on Tuesday and block the exact same request on Wednesday if conditions look anomalous,” the report notes.

AI is being used to speed up the development and deployment of new software, and in 2027, security will have to become a continuous system embedded in the software delivery pipeline, according to Google.

In a recent development, threat actors have carried out software supply chain attacks over the years, one of the most notable being the SolarWinds incident of 2020. Sandra Joyce, VP of Google Threat Intelligence, says cybercriminals are now poisoning everything from open-source code to software libraries, which AI coding assistants often pull automatically into codebases.

Also: How AI security failures are endangering your supply chain.

Bug-fix tickets that take days to respond to and security appearing at the end of a software development cycle no longer work. Instead, writing and securing code must happen simultaneously, with the help of agentic AI, so speed doesn’t compromise security.

“It’s also crucial that we link live production environments directly back to source code so that defenders can trace a real-world exposure to the exact line of code, validate whether it is genuinely exploitable, and deliver a pre-tested fix at machine speed without breaking production,” Google added.

As organizations rush to implement AI into their applications and services to appear “AI-first,” innovative, and modern, security may be ignored or treated as an afterthought.

In a recent development, as a result, we may face a new, broader attack surface than we realize, as AI introduces new security concerns, including software vulnerabilities, misconfiguration, bypasses, and indirect prompt injection attacks. Now that AI is also in the hands of all cyberattackers — from script kiddies to state-sponsored groups — auditing corporate networks and infrastructure is crucial.

Industry observers note that also: Who’s responsible for catching rogue AI agents? You are.

According to recent reports, penetration testing and red team exercises now need to cover agentic AI. This wasn’t in scope for many red teams only a few years ago, but now that businesses have run with the idea of implementing AI in their workflows, processes, and products, organizations need to identify and fix security problems introduced by AI before threat actors take advantage of them.

CISOs should task pen testers with auditing before an autonomous workflow hits production, then combine the results with threat intelligence to ensure defenders have the information they need to bolster network defenses and harden classifiers against latest and novel attacks.

The final significant trend we are likely to see in 2027 is tackling agent sprawl to create coordinated teams of AI agents that can rapidly handle security tasks at scale.

It has been revealed that single AI agents given general instructions won’t cut it when AI-assisted attackers can compromise endpoint devices, enter networks, move laterally, or start stealing data in a far shorter timeframe than before. Instead, CISOs should replace these “generalist” AI agents with specialized, orchestrated teams of AI agents that can meet the demands of defending against AI-driven attacks by employing specialist tooling and skill sets.

Also: AI agent kill switch urged by Okta-led alliance.

Recent findings suggest that CISOs also need to ensure that each agent has its own domain training and understanding, memory, and dedicated tools, and can act on its own within set limits, with a central coordinator that knows when to hand a decision to a human. This requires oversight, but in return, organizations will avoid agent sprawl, which the tech giant believes is the next iteration of shadow IT and its associated threats.

Dutch Bros generates higher net profit and stronger operating margins than CAVA, and profit is growing faster than sales, indicating the business gets more profitable as it scales. And the stock trades at a discount to CAVA on forward earnings and sales.

In a recent development, both of these companies are resonating with consumers and growing rapidly, but the restaurant business is highly competitive and breaking ground on latest locations is cost-intensive. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that now that the iPhone Duo is in stores, there are plenty of people who are curious about Apple’s first folding device.
  • If you’re planning on checking out the iPhone Duo at the Apple store, it might be easy to just marvel at how cool it looks, but if you’re considering making this your fresh phone that’ll be in your pocket all of the time, you’ll probably want to get an idea of how it will be living with this new design.
  • Below, we’ve listed a handful of features and things to try out when you’re test-driving the Apple iPhone Duo in the store.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that now that the iPhone Duo is in stores, there are plenty of people who are curious about Apple’s first folding device. Foldables are hardly a latest sector in the smartphone world, with Samsung leading the charge, but Apple’s entry into the market is a substantial deal, and the iPhone Duo is a stunner.

If you’re planning on checking out the iPhone Duo at the Apple store, it might be easy to just marvel at how cool it looks, but if you’re considering making this your fresh phone that’ll be in your pocket all of the time, you’ll probably want to get an idea of how it will be living with this new design. After all, you should be in love with all aspects of the device if you’re going to drop $2,000-plus on it.

Below, we’ve listed a handful of features and things to try out when you’re test-driving the Apple iPhone Duo in the store.

Industry observers note that when the Duo was first revealed, Apple showed off a very intriguing animation when you unfold it. Leave it to Apple to make a function so simple look so aesthetically pleasing.

In a recent development, it’ll likely be the first thing you notice when you first open the Duo up to see its inner display, and there’s a good chance you’ll continue to open and close the device to see the effect. At the end of the day, it’s a parlor trick — but a very good one, adding delight to ordinary use.

Read more: The iPhone Duo Crossed 517,000 Folds and Counting in Our Custom Machine.

Foldables, well, fold, and they typically come with creases. The Duo has a minimal crease and a matte display, both of which are wins. That noted, even the most noticeable creases tend to “disappear” when you’re viewing content — you just get used to them while watching TV shows or YouTube videos. The Duo’s minimal crease should be even easier to ignore.

Recent findings suggest that and let’s not forget about the matte screen. Several foldables ship with glossy displays, but the iPhone Duo will have a less shiny screen, making it easier to view in bright environments without annoying reflections.

The outer passport-size display on the iPhone Duo may be a little awkward for watching videos because of how it crops content to fit the fresh aspect ratio. Still, it’s handy to prop the phone up in tent mode and watch shows that way. You also have a large inner display to work with, but because of its passport-style design, even that screen has a different aspect ratio than the widescreen format people are used to on regular phones, so there will likely be some letterboxing in videos.

Try watching something with the phone set up in both ways to see if it bothers you enough to dissuade you from buying the phone.

Again, it’s not an iPhone Duo issue but a foldable phone issue — the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 is the same size and format. The aspect ratio of the display might crop the top or sides of videos, so it’s worth trying out if you expect to watch a lot of full-screen videos.

Recent findings suggest that like videos, apps on foldables can sometimes appear a little weird, and that could be the case with the iPhone Duo‘s aspect ratio. When you’re at the Apple Store, check out how your most-used apps look and feel on both the inner and outer displays, and make sure you rotate the inner screen to see how apps behave in this orientation, too — that wide screen could be great for watching vertical videos or scrolling through social media.

Sources indicate that if some apps, such as Instagram, look a little different or are wonky, it’ll hopefully be just a matter of time until the developers make an update that optimizes the experience for this latest design. Keep in mind that you can also have two apps open onscreen at once, making it easier to multitask.

If you want the best camera experience on an iPhone right now, you should be looking at the iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max, but that doesn’t make the Duo a slouch for shooting photos, either.

Industry observers note that yes, the Duo is missing a third camera (telephoto), and if that’s important to you, then you probably shouldn’t even be considering Apple’s foldable. But still, if you’re going to shell out this much money for a newly introduced phone, test out those cameras — even if it’s in a controlled environment like an Apple Store.

Recent findings suggest that another thing to check out before you pull the trigger is your selfie shots with this latest phone. There are two main ways to do this: with the phone closed, holding it up in the regular way you’d take a selfie using the outer screen’s 12-megapixel front-facing camera, or with the inner display open and shooting with the twin 48-megapixel rear cameras (the outer screen will show a preview of the shot).

Recent findings suggest that there’s also a front-facing camera underneath the inner display, which is mostly for video calls — and which we suspect would produce the least-impressive shots from the device. Try them all and see what you think of the pics. And since you’re at an Apple Store, make sure you delete them afterward.

The odd but interesting aspect ratio of the front display on the iPhone Duo may be a little awkward for typing, so it’s best to do a typing test when you have one in front of you. While the inner display will provide a roomier and more comfortable typing experience, you probably won’t want to have to open up the Duo every time you want to shoot off a quick text to someone. If you have bigger hands, typing on the front screen could be a bit of a nightmare.

Typing one-handed on the small cover screen should be manageable, but try it out to see if it works for you. Some may find it convenient; others may find it cumbersome.

Recent findings suggest that and when you’re typing on the inner display, try the Duo in both portrait and landscape orientations to see which feels better. You can also choose between a split keyboard and larger keys. It’s thoughtful of Apple to offer options that let you tailor the typing experience to your preferences, but you may find that none of them suit your style.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that apple is exploring how people use AI for their health, presumably to build its own AI health coach. On Sunday, it debuted the Apple Health AI Usage Study, which could contribute to the next AI health experience Apple builds by measuring the quality of AI health responses, comprehension, and everyday health behaviors, according to a press release.

Sources indicate that apple is conducting the study in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform widely used by healthcare professionals. The study examines the relationship between conversational AI tools, like chatbots, and the people who use them.

“Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey,” Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness, remarked in the press release.

Also: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Finally, the health tracker I’ve been waiting for.

According to recent reports, participants are encouraged to share their HealthKit data and query the health app with questions. The study will also explore how AI tools can best prepare patients ahead of clinical visits. Apple will monitor the AI’s clarity and approachability when providing medical information, and each response or recommendation will be linked to peer-reviewed clinical citations. Responses could be unclear or incomplete, which is why Apple is rolling this out as a study to explore a responsibly designed AI health assistant.

Recent findings suggest that apple often debuts studies for features it would like to develop in the future. For example, many of the hearing health features debuted on the AirPods were a direct result of the findings from Apple’s Hearing Study.

Also: Athenahealth patients can ask Claude about their medical records now.

According to recent reports, the AI usage study comes on the heels of the revamped Health app’s debut, which introduces officially next month. It also arrives amid a bevy of AI health coaches, popping up alongside companion health devices. Google launched its AI Health Coach in Google Health Premium last year, and Oura launched a proprietary AI model for women trained on medical standards and research from Oura’s in-house team of board-certified clinicians.

A growing number of Americans are relying on AI for medical advice. A recent survey from Pew Research Center found that 34% of US adults have talked with a chatbot for medical advice. As AI proliferates, that percentage will only increase.

According to recent reports, “Patients and clinicians are both turning to AI, but the tools they use are being built and tested in separate worlds,” said Robert M. Wachter, M.D., UCSF’s professor and chair of the Department of Medicine, in the press release.

Apple and other tech companies are building for this new health normal, and the AI usage study indicates that Apple isn’t taking the responsibility lightly.

According to recent reports, if you’re interested in participating in Apple’s study, it’s open to 200,000 eligible participants age 21 and older in the US. You’ll need a phone with Apple Intelligence enabled (the iPhone 15 Pro or later), running iOS 26 or later. You can download the study app to learn more and enroll.

10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.

The Anthropic (ANT +0.00%) initial public offering (IPO) is a landmark moment for artificial intelligence (AI) investing and sheds further light on the interrelationships among AI companies. One of these is Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +1.60%), which is set to receive a large share of the $900.9 billion in spending commitments outlined in Anthropic's latest Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings.

In a recent development, most of Anthropic's expenditure relates to compute and infrastructure, with up to $120.5 billion allocated to SpaceX's SpaceXAI subsidiary. The terms extend through 2029, with about $3.1 billion payable per month after capacity is delivered. Anthropic expects that to occur beginning in December.

Interestingly, both parties have the right to cancel the agreement with 90 days' notice, but this only kicks in after a noncancellable period, which ends in January 2027 and March 2027. In theory, at least, this means Anthropic could write to SpaceX on Feb. 1 and on April 1 to initiate cancellation of the agreements 90 days after those dates.

This is notable because Anthropic's spending commitments with Microsoft (up to $49.2 billion), Alphabet's Google ($121.3 billion), and Amazon (at least $110 billion) are all noncancelable unless there's a material breach of the agreement.

NASDAQ · As of 9:41 AM ET 11/19/26.

Industry observers note that revenue from Anthropic is significant, validating SpaceX's vast AI infrastructure investments and strengthening its financial position ahead of any potential merger with Tesla. That mentioned, investors will have to keep an eye on developments, as Anthropic's ability to cancel the agreement means SpaceX is first in line to suffer should Anthropic decrease its investment looks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Oura developed a tool for its frequent-flying members that could help them stave off the worst of jet lag.

Ahead of the busy holiday travel season, on Tuesday, Oura announced Jet Lag Plan, a new feature designed to help travelers feel alert and energized after crossing several time zones.

Also: Oura Ring users may get in-app access to real doctors soon – what we know.

Jet Lag Plan takes into account your travel itinerary, sleep patterns, and body responses to provide guidance for traveling members entering newly introduced time zones.

Jet lag happens when circadian rhythms are at odds with local time zones, but there are a few things people can do to adjust.

Oura factors in the direction of travel, how many time zones are crossed, individual light windows, and sleep timing.

In a recent development, ring users will enter their flight details, including information like multi-stop trips, and also include the reason for the trip. Oura adjusts the Jet Lag Plan accordingly, and a business trip’s plan may differ in intensity from that of a vacation.

In a recent development, “Two people on the same flight can get different intends, because guidance reflects your itinerary, your typical sleep schedule, and your chronotype,” Oura writes in a blog post. The chronotype refers to Oura’s sleep chronotype, which categorizes owners into six types (early morning, morning, early evening, and so on) based on their historical sleep activity.

Also: I wore the Oura Ring 5 for a month.

In a recent development, after adding these details, Oura provides each user with timely guidance throughout their trip. This guidance could include recommendations on when to begin or end caffeine consumption or light exposure, and when to start preparing for sleep. The proposal is designed for those crossing three or more time zones. Members can follow along with these recommendations by checking them off as they complete each one. People can also talk to Oura’s Advisor in the event of flight or timing changes.

Jet Lag Plan is now available for Oura Members with Oura Ring Gen 3 or later.

Go to your home screen, tap the + and select Jet Lag Strategy to get started. You can also tell Oura Advisor about a trip to initiate Jet Lag Plan. If the Oura app detects a time zone shift of 3 or more hours, Jet Lag Plan may appear as a push notification.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In iOS 27, Apple announced iPhone Handoff, a networking feature that allows users to switch cell service between two eSIM-enabled iPhones.
  • Sources indicate that code strings include “Use a SIM on two phones,” and note that the feature will be called Fast Switch.
  • Also: Why your USB-C cables look alike, but work differently – and how to tell them apart.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In iOS 27, Apple announced iPhone Handoff, a networking feature that allows users to switch cell service between two eSIM-enabled iPhones. Text strings in Google’s SIM Manager app suggest the company is preparing a similar feature for compatible Android phones, according to Android Authority.

Sources indicate that code strings include “Use a SIM on two phones,” and note that the feature will be called Fast Switch. Little information is currently available about the feature’s limitations, including which phones or mobile carriers may not be compatible.

Also: Why your USB-C cables look alike, but work differently – and how to tell them apart.

On Apple’s side, any iPhone in the US running iOS 27 with a T-Mobile or Verizon-provided eSIM can use iPhone Handoff. AT&T does not at the moment support iPhone Handoff.

However, the code strings uncovered by Android Authority show that Android’s Fast Switch will work similarly to iPhone Handoff, in that customers must be signed in to both devices under the same Google account for the feature to work.

Strings in Google’s SIM Manager app also point to no sharing between two users, so this feature isn’t a way to circumvent carrier fees by adding service to someone else’s phone for the price of one.

Sources indicate that if Fast Switch works anything like iPhone Handoff, which it appears it will, one eSIM can be switched between two phones. So, calls, messages, location services, and other information synced to your Apple ID can remain consistent between two devices.

Also: 5 hidden iOS 27 features that make older iPhones better.

Some third-party apps, like banking, communications, or social media, may also remain consistent across the two phones, depending on the app’s syncing behavior.

In a recent development, features like Apple’s iPhone Handoff and Google’s Fast Switch are ideal for people who regularly use two phones. Business owners and digital creators may want one phone strictly for business purposes and the other for personal use.

Also: Google Wallet turns your Android phone into a digital house key.

In that case, one person can keep up with two phones without paying for two phone service lines through their carrier. Still, customers will incur a fee, as T-Mobile charges $5/month for iPhone Handoff, while Verizon charges $10/month.

Latest Update: Nvidia’s Earnings Calmed Markets, but AI’s Harsh Reckoning Marches On

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1299 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Though Nvidia’s earnings call Tuesday offered some reassurance to investors after Jensen Huang’s departure as CEO, it did little to resolve the political, regulatory and leadership questions hanging over the entire AI economy.
  • The semiconductor giant at the heart of the AI infrastructure boom saw its shares plunge by 35% from last month’s high following the scandal around Huang — wiping out nearly $2 trillion in market cap and triggering Wall Street panic around a broader AI reckoning.
  • Industry observers note that nvidia’s finance chief and interim CEO, Colette Kress, sought to project stability, telling investors it was “business as usual” and raising Nvidia’s fiscal 2028 outlook.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Though Nvidia’s earnings call Tuesday offered some reassurance to investors after Jensen Huang’s departure as CEO, it did little to resolve the political, regulatory and leadership questions hanging over the entire AI economy.

The semiconductor giant at the heart of the AI infrastructure boom saw its shares plunge by 35% from last month’s high following the scandal around Huang — wiping out nearly $2 trillion in market cap and triggering Wall Street panic around a broader AI reckoning.

Industry observers note that nvidia’s finance chief and interim CEO, Colette Kress, sought to project stability, telling investors it was “business as usual” and raising Nvidia’s fiscal 2028 outlook. Though the chipmaker’s stock price rebounded after reporting better-than-expected results, it’s likely to face a rocky future, as concerns linger around national security violations amid illegal export deals. Market confidence is also shaky amid supply chain backlogs for advanced chips and servers that remain critical to AI compute and the training of large language models.

According to recent reports, in the lead-up to the manufacturer’s third-quarter earnings call, Huang issued a statement that he would return as CEO if the board of directors decides it’s in the “best interest” of shareholders and the country. Despite calls from President Donald Trump and other tech executives to reinstate the former GPU boss, Harvey C. Jones, Nvidia’s appointed first-ever chair of the board, said there is no intention to reinstate Huang, and no successor was named.

Prior to the call, The Wall Street Journal reported that the US Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating Huang over concerns that the company misled investors.

Huang maneuvered Nvidia into a linchpin role for frontier AI labs and data center firms, not just by supplying hardware but also by providing equity, credit and financial backing and by mobilizing third-party capital to secure investment for the AI buildout of data centers. Nvidia’s circular financing schemes — in which the chipmaker helps fund a hyperscaler like Meta or Microsoft, which then uses the funds to buy its products — were allegedly a source of contention for Kress and other executives.

Critics have warned that this kind of vendor financing inflated the AI bubble by inflating growth projections and buoying the market valuations of chipmakers and hyperscalers.

According to Reuters, Kress was expected to pull back from some of the riskiest AI financial deals, including investments in OpenAI and AI infrastructure companies such as Lambda. Already, Nvidia has significantly scaled back financing for a $250 billion OpenAI data center deal. During Tuesday’s call, Kress failed to announce a sweeping unwind of Huang-era financing arrangements, focusing more on continuity than retreat.

Industry observers note that kress mentioned that chip producer TSMC, a key Nvidia partner, will continue working with Nvidia despite Huang’s departure. The company also noted it was assuming no China data-center compute revenue in its next fourth-quarter outlook.

It has been revealed that nvidia supplies the lion’s share of the hardware necessary for data center construction and model training, and the organization has long noted that the demand for chips exceeds supply. Shortages of RAM and high-bandwidth memory slow down the production of AI servers and raise prices for cloud companies and other buyers. In an attempt to buy its way out of the bottleneck, Nvidia has committed large sums of money to secure future memory supply.

Industry observers note that if Nvidia distances itself too much from its GPU commitments, that could be a problem for the entire tech industry. Semiconductor production is an incredibly specialized field dominated by very few companies, and any changes to the supply chain could have ripple effects on global markets and vendors, including in consumer electronics and cloud services.

Huang’s affair with a Chinese executive connected to the Singapore-based Megaspeed — whom US intelligence claimed was a Chinese intelligence asset — complicated an already tight supply chain. Megaspeed was under investigation for allegedly helping Chinese firms obtain high-value Nvidia chips through channels that violated US export controls.

According to the investment research firm Culper, up to one-fifth of Nvidia’s fiscal-year 2026 compute revenues were driven by movement of some of the company’s most advanced chips into China through nonrestricted intermediary countries in a process called diversion. When advanced Nvidia chips or servers are illegally routed to Chinese buyers, those units are no longer available to legal customers in the US and allied markets.

Industry observers note that huang was influential in shaping the Trump administration’s chip export policies, pushing back against export controls that limited Nvidia’s sales to China. But the recent scandal prompted upcoming Commerce Department restrictions on chip shipments through third countries.

While Kress cited improving supply and sustained demand in raising Nvidia’s outlook, stricter export rules and tighter controls could further constrain capacity by creating more obstacles to compliance and delivery.

Nvidia’s better-than-expected earnings may steady investors in the short term, but any organization that supplies essential hardware for the AI buildout is at risk if investor confidence in the industry falters. When Nvidia reports strong growth, AI-focused stocks and funds with large technology holdings are likely to go up. When Nvidia’s outlook weakens, investors worry that AI spending is slowing or that companies have overcommitted.

It has been revealed that A handful of major tech companies — colloquially known as the Magnificent Seven — make up a big share of major funds and indices. Five of them account for roughly 30% of the S&P 500 index, and AI overexposure in those businesses translates into overexposure in many individual retirement accounts and 401(k)s. Because index funds hold substantial positions in Nvidia and other large tech companies, an AI selloff could affect retirement balances even for people who don’t own Nvidia shares directly.

It has been revealed that the Magnificent Seven are heavily affected by AI stock swings. Alphabet’s stock price sank as Nvidia news aftershocks reverberated through the markets, proving that top firms are not unassailable. Other tech companies heavily focused on AI infrastructure, such as Intel and CoreWeave, likewise saw their share prices decline.

Industry observers note that despite growing concerns about AI dangers, Huang was one of AI’s most aggressive promoters, framing the technology as an economic and national security imperative. In early September, the now-disgraced CEO mentioned that artificial general intelligence, or AGI, had arrived, congratulating OpenAI on its GPT-6 Astra model, which was trained on Nvidia’s Grace Blackwell GPUs.

Huang pushed against recent warnings from AI researchers, calling for unrestrained progress on frontier models and repeatedly arguing against fresh laws and safety regulations.

Even before Huang’s business and personal scandals came to light, AI companies were gearing up for a post-midterm-election PR campaign, as the technology has become increasingly unpopular and the backlash against data centers has grown. Democratic Party politicians pushed a platform to shift the federal government’s lax approach toward the AI industry. Some Democrats are also poised to craft legislation to prevent an AI industry bailout in the event of a bubble pop.

Amid bipartisan calls for Huang to testify before Congress, many politicians are also seeking to investigate high-ranking members of US intelligence and the Commerce Department for allowing export loopholes or for failing to act on knowledge of Nvidia’s China-related deals.

Kress might be able to lead Nvidia with tact and diligence, separating the tech giant from some of its riskiest deals. But the national security implications of her predecessor’s relationships have opened up a can of worms that no CEO can close on their own.

In a recent development, the federal government is ruled by inertia, but right now there’s some investigative momentum aimed directly at the major AI players. That will almost certainly ice out some investor hype. It’s clear the AI industry is facing a reckoning that was not in the cards just months ago.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage rose to 7.34% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is seven basis points higher than yesterday and 34 basis points higher than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

In a recent development, mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

On Friday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics released the Producer Price Index for October, which tracks the change in prices that U.S. producers are able to get for their products. This is one way to measure inflation on the market end, rather than the consumer end.

The results were mixed. While prices didn’t rise quite as high as economists anticipated month-over-month (0.3% vs. 0.4%), year-over-year price growth did reach 6.5% — the largest increase in four years. This points to even higher costs for consumers coming in the near future.

Investors are convinced that the Federal Reserve will raise overnight borrowing rates again in December to pull inflation down. And higher overnight borrowing rates — called the federal funds rate, which is what banks pay to fund products like mortgages — usually lead to higher mortgage rates.

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you strategy to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

What Berkshire Hathaway's Third-Quarter Report Notes About Its Insurance Business

💡 Key Takeaways
  • 10 stocks we like better than Berkshire Hathaway ›.
  • It's been roughly two weeks since Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA -1.29%) (BRKB -1.03%) posted its third-quarter results.
  • Berkshire's insurance business, which -- depending on the quarter -- can be the company's single-biggest source of operating income.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By James Brumley – Nov 19, 2026 at 5:30AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Berkshire Hathaway ›.

It's been roughly two weeks since Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA -1.29%) (BRKB -1.03%) posted its third-quarter results. And yet, there's still plenty about this complex conglomerate's numbers left to dissect.

Today's topic? Berkshire's insurance business, which -- depending on the quarter -- can be the company's single-biggest source of operating income. Only this time around, it suffered a measurable dip in the bottom line.

Industry observers note that you may know it best as a collection of Warren Buffett-approved stock picks. That's hardly all that Berkshire Hathaway is, however. It owns several dozen privately held businesses like Shaw flooring, Duracell batteries, railroad BNSF, Pilot Travel Centers, Clayton Homes, and GEICO insurance, just to name a few. These outfits collectively make up about 40% of Berkshire's total market value of $1.25 trillion and account for all of its operating income, which is on pace to reach $48 billion to $50 billion this year alone.

Sources indicate that and insurance is a huge piece of this profit. Between underwriting and investment income stemming from its insurance business, this arm delivered nearly 45% of last year's operating earnings.

Recent findings suggest that this year, though, isn't nearly as impressive. Through the first three quarters of the year, insurance-related investment income of just under $8.5 billion is down 10% from year-earlier comparisons, while underwriting income of $4.8 billion is lower to the tune of almost 16%.

Image source: Chart by author. Data from Berkshire Hathaway.

GEICO is a key contributor to this weakness. After a couple of banner years, it was finally forced to increase commissions for brokers and agents as well as advertise more. Claim numbers are also up, reflecting the growing price of ... well, everything.

It's not just the insurance-specific aspect of this arm, however, that's running into a headwind. Berkshire also earns money on the cash it keeps on hand to pay claims. While they're up now, the lower interest rates compared to earlier this year are still taking their toll. Indeed, practically all of this year's 10.3% dip in Berkshire's insurance-related investment income is the result of lower interest rates on shorter-term bonds, which were higher at this point last year.

So what do Berkshire Hathaway's Q3 numbers say about its insurance business? A lot. More than anything, however, it indicates this business isn't exactly consistent even if its ebbs and flows are somewhat predictable from one quarter to the next.

Oh, certainly experienced investors have seen more erratic income trends. By some standards, in fact, Berkshire's insurance operation actually is reasonably consistent.

NYSE · As of 9:40 AM ET 11/19/26.

For Berkshire Hathaway and its shareholders, though, this isn't the sort of inconsistency that's easy to digest from one quarter to the next. The other businesses it also owns don't necessarily offset its insurance operation's earnings headwinds at the right time either, as Berkshire's erratic total operating earnings data, plotted on the chart above, indicates us.

Just don't lose sight of the bigger picture. One disappointing quarter -- or even one disappointing year -- doesn't necessarily mean this business is being poorly managed. The longer-term growth trend here is far more important, and it still looks fine even if the recent post-earnings rhetoric hasn't been overwhelmingly bullish.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google’s Gemini can now turn your notes and other sources in your Gemini Notebook (previously called NotebookLM) into interactive pages or sites to help you better process complicated information.

Complete with flashcards, dashboards, and colorful panels, the sites make it easier to study and understand intricate concepts. I tested the feature, unveiled Tuesday, to see how efficient it is at creating a navigable site that is actually helpful and stays loyal to sources.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s latest Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector in my tests.

Because Notebooks are built with the sources you provide, like textbooks, files, or notes, the sites are created with the data that is in your Gemini Notebook. Notebook has three tabs: Sources, Chat, and Studio. The site option is in the Studio tab, listed under what you can create.

If you’re taking a college class, you could put all the information you need to prepare for a test and use the interactive site as a study guide that you can share with others.

To test this, I gave Notebook the following prompt:.

“Make me a site that visually explains how cellular respiration works, breaking down each stage with interactive diagrams and self-check flashcards.”.

Since I’m not in a class that would give me those study materials, I gave Gemini online sources to use for this. Gemini cited the sources in my notebook, then spent a few minutes creating the interactive site. Gemini will give you a quick update when it’s done, including a summary of the source information as it pertains to your request and instructions on where to find the site.

Also: I checked Gemini’s newly introduced Memory summary to see what it knew about me – how to see and edit yours.

As promised, my cellular respiration notes were complete and organized on an interactive, visually appealing site that was easy to navigate. The coolest feature on the site was the flashcards, which you can hover over to see which ones you’ve studied.

The interactive site feature is now available to Gemini Notebook users and will soon come to the mobile app. As someone who knows very little about coding, I was pretty satisfied to see the information Gemini put together presented in explorable, easy-to-understand tabs on a site.

#39202. Fathom Forthcoming: First Battery Cells Roll Out of Ford’s Michigan Plant for Electric Pickup

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1277 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Fathom Forthcoming: First Battery Cells Roll Out of Ford’s Michigan Plant for Electric Pickup

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1277 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This week, Ford began shipments of the first lithium iron phosphate electric vehicle battery cells from its fresh BlueOval Battery Park in Marshall, Michigan, to its Louisville Assembly Plant in Kentucky.
  • In 2025, consumers lost access to the clean vehicle tax rebates of the Inflation Reduction Act, but the program and its incentives remain in the law for automakers and suppliers.
  • Ford expects to sell the upcoming Fathom at an estimated price of $28,350 (well, $29,945, including the $1,595 destination and delivery fee), with the first preorder expected to open early next year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This week, Ford began shipments of the first lithium iron phosphate electric vehicle battery cells from its fresh BlueOval Battery Park in Marshall, Michigan, to its Louisville Assembly Plant in Kentucky. There, the prismatic cells will power early Ford Fathom electric pickup truck prototypes and validation vehicles. The automaker invited me into the plant to meet the people who build the batteries and to see how the so-called “jelly roll” is made.

In 2025, consumers lost access to the clean vehicle tax rebates of the Inflation Reduction Act, but the program and its incentives remain in the law for automakers and suppliers. So bringing this US-based, domestically owned battery plant online is kind of a big deal for Ford. It’s an crucial milestone for the automaker’s plan to make its fresh Universal Electric Vehicle, or UEV, platform a reality and to bring the Fathom — its upcoming electric pickup truck — to market in 2027 at a price that EV-eager customers can stomach.

Ford expects to sell the upcoming Fathom at an estimated price of $28,350 (well, $29,945, including the $1,595 destination and delivery fee), with the first preorder expected to open early next year.

In a recent development, blueOval Battery Park Michigan is a $3 billion, 2 million-square-foot facility with a targeted annual production capacity of 20 gigawatt-hours. That’s a whole lot of batteries. Ford is expected to employ 1,700 people at the site across two 12-hour shifts, running around the clock to reach that capacity.

According to recent reports, the plant is a clean facility, so getting in meant donning a clean suit, mask, hairnet, gloves and two layers of shoe booties. I then crossed special magnetic and sticky floor panels designed to pull any metal particles off the bottoms of those booties, before passing through multiple air-blower airlocks that blasted my body clean of loose dust.

From the outside, the building is huge and difficult to take in completely. On the inside, the scale truly comes into focus as I stare down a massive hallway just under a mile long end to end. Raw materials — rolls of copper and aluminum sheet, plus the chemical powders that coat them — enter the plant at the eastern end, move in a straight line through the facility, and completed battery packs exit at the western end. The first 0.7 mile of the fab belongs to cell production, split between isolated cathode and anode lines that join halfway through for final cell assembly.

Ford engineers, battery experts and executives tell me that the automaker chose lithium iron phosphate, or LFP, chemistry in a prismatic (rectangular) format for its affordability and structural benefits. LFP uses no nickel or cobalt, which keeps costs down, and Ford found the chemistry well suited to bidirectional charging.

In a recent development, to keep costs low enough to deliver a reasonably priced car, Ford couldn’t use a Chinese supplier and still qualify for IRA manufacturing credits. So it licensed the technology from one, working with a company called CATL, which one Ford exec described as “the world’s leading battery manufacturer,” whose batteries power 30 million vehicles worldwide.

Despite working with a Chinese firm, Ford notes the plant is completely US-owned, staffed and operated and is totally IRA-compliant, with no foreign entity of concern, or FEOC, involvement beyond the licensing agreement.

Charles Poon, who leads vehicle hardware engineering, said Ford didn’t simply copy a catalog part.

“We designed a unique cell that does not exist in the CATL catalog, specifically for the UEV,” Poon remarked, adding that the taller and simpler cell delivers “the energy density, the affordability, the durability that [Ford is] looking for” and allows the automaker to more completely integrate the cells and battery pack into the vehicle’s design.

Ford also had to build the supply chain, Poon stated, sourcing an IRA-compliant stream for a battery chemistry that is only just entering the mainstream in North America, and working with approved global partners and North American suppliers.

Recent findings suggest that on the cathode and anode assembly lines, meter-wide rolls of copper and aluminum are first coated with a chemical slurry that is baked on. The large rolls are then split into 10 smaller rolls, with tabs notched into their exposed edges at set intervals. As the continuous rolls pass through multiple machines like gigantic cassette players, AI-powered vision systems watch the foil for coating defects, scratches and wrinkles, marking problem sections so they can be automatically removed.

According to recent reports, next, the cathode and anode foils are layered and rolled into a cylinder, then pressed flat into what Ford calls a jelly roll. Imagine a roll of toilet paper mashed in a hydraulic press, and you’ll have a good idea of what it looks like: a flat rectangle with rounded ends.

In a recent development, the jelly rolls are then gathered in pairs, and the previously exposed tabs are folded together and ultrasonically welded to more solid terminals, which are in turn laser-welded to a cap. The jelly roll couple is then laser-sealed into an aluminum box, about the size and weight of a masonry brick, to form a nearly complete prismatic cell. Engineers vacuum out the air, check for leaks by pressurizing the cell with helium, and fill it with liquid electrolyte. Bob’s your uncle: you have a finished LFP prismatic cell.

Ford notes the assembly lines can deliver 40 cells every minute, which plant manager Tracy Church says makes BlueOval Battery Park “among the fastest LFP prismatic lines outside China.”.

In a recent development, from the cell line, completed prismatic cells would normally pass through a door and straight into pack manufacturing, where full battery packs with integrated “e-box” electronics, integrated cooling and wiring are built. That part of the plant is still undergoing validation, so for now Ford is shipping just the cells to Louisville, not complete battery packs. The firm prepares to have pack manufacturing up and running in Marshall ahead of Fathom’s launch, with full pack deliveries to Louisville planned in 2027. Church told me that the plant aims to produce 50 battery packs per hour.

Ford hasn’t officially specified the energy capacity of the cells or the completed battery packs and wouldn’t comment when asked about expected range for the Fathom. The automaker wouldn’t even confirm how many cells go into the EV’s pack, but I estimate between 90 and 108 cells based on a cutaway of the finalized unit I examined (but wasn’t permitted to photograph) during my tour. I expect Ford is holding off on finalizing details until closer to the EV’s 2027 launch window.

It has been revealed that battery Park Michigan isn’t just sending cells to Kentucky; it’s also sending expertise. Ford’s Glendale Kentucky plant — which used to build batteries for the F-150 Lightning full-size electric pickup — is at the moment being retooled to build LFP cells for Ford Energy for large-scale energy storage applications, and the lessons Ford learns in Michigan are already being shared with the manufacturing teams there.

Recent findings suggest that ford has been in the EV business for over 15 years. In 2011, it revealed the Focus Electric at CES. 2019 brought the debut of the Mustang Mach-E — which Ford recently found is holding up well after years on the road with minimal battery degradation — followed by the arrival of the F-150 Lightning in 2021. This isn’t the brand’s first electric rodeo, but executives tell me that the automaker has never had this much control and ownership over its battery production, and it’s hoping that will make the difference as it prepares the next-gen UEV vehicles.

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (787 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

The Stock Market Is Sounding an Alarm, But History Has Good News for Investors

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (787 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • 10 stocks we like better than SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust ›.
  • Two of Wall Street's best-known valuation metrics are both signaling warnings.
  • The Shiller cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings (CAPE) ratio, which measures the value of the S&P 500 (^GSPC +0.81%) relative to inflation-adjusted earnings over the past 10 years, is at 40 right now.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By David Dierking – Nov 19, 2026 at 5:45AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust ›.

Two of Wall Street's best-known valuation metrics are both signaling warnings.

The Shiller cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings (CAPE) ratio, which measures the value of the S&P 500 (^GSPC +0.81%) relative to inflation-adjusted earnings over the past 10 years, is at 40 right now. The only other time it was at this level in the past 150 years was during the peak of the 2000 tech bubble.

The Buffett indicator, named for a metric popularized by Warren Buffett that measures the value of U.S. stocks relative to U.S. gross domestic product (GDP), is also at (or near) all-time highs. That number is around 250%, far above where it's been at any point in its history.

A lot of headlines suggest that these are potential disaster signals for the market. But they're not predictors. They're merely valuation measures, and as we've seen over the past several years, high valuations don't mean they can't go higher.

In fact, there's good news to be found in some other financial metrics.

You probably know what happened following the tech bubble peak. After a record high in March 2000, it took the S&P 500 roughly 13 years to reach another fresh all-time high that it was able to sustain (It hit a new high in October 2007, but the Great Recession busted it down again almost immediately).

The Shiller CAPE ratio went from 44 at the tech bubble peak all the way down to 14 at the financial crisis bottom, the lowest it had been to that point since the 1980s.

The Buffett indicator nearly touched 150% during the tech bubble peak, which was a record at the time, but it briefly fell below 60% during the financial crisis. The Buffett indicator did, however, hit a newly introduced all-time high back in the late 2010s and has headed steadily higher since. The only real interruption was the 2022 bear market.

Here's the good news. If you look at the time frame from the peak of the tech bubble through today, the S&P 500 is up just over 700%. That translates to around 8% growth annually. Yes, even with 13 years of essentially no return on investment, an investment in large-cap U.S. stocks still produced an average annual return that wasn't that far off from its long-term average of 10%.

NYSEMKT · As of 9:38 AM ET 11/19/26.

I'd reiterate that the Shiller CAPE ratio and the Buffett indicator are valuation measures. They're not recession predictors or bear market signals. They simply tell you how expensive stocks are relative to a baseline at any moment in time.

It has been revealed that plus, these two numbers aren't the only way to value the U.S. stock market. If you consider the forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, which looks at forecasted earnings for the next year, the State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY +0.97%) trades at just 19 times the next 12 months' earnings. That's the lowest it's been since the end of 2023. The Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (RSP -0.12%) trades at a forward P/E ratio of just 16.7.

In other words, not every valuation measure is flashing warnings. If companies can deliver on earnings over the next 12 months, there's no reason to think that a big valuation contraction is imminent.

I wouldn't make any radical changes to your portfolio's asset allocation. If you'd sold stocks when valuations looked high over the past several years, you would have missed out on a gain of more than 100% since the beginning of 2023 for the S&P 500.

It has been revealed that the biggest takeaway is that nobody knows what stocks will do next. So there's little sense in trying to trade your brokerage account as if you do. As long as your long-term asset allocation is consistent with your long-term goals, there's little reason to make any major changes to it.

Industry observers note that the S&P 500 still works well as a portfolio core. Even if the index does fall sharply from here, continuing with regular contributions into your brokerage or retirement accounts can help buy shares at discount prices, lower your average cost basis, and actually improve your portfolio's long-term returns.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google likes to use your conversations with Gemini for model training to help improve the AI.
  • Also: I checked Gemini’s fresh Memory summary to see what it knew about me.
  • Sources indicate that in a change set to roll out in the coming weeks, you’ll be able to put the brakes on Gemini model training without losing access to your previous conversations with the AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google likes to use your conversations with Gemini for model training to help improve the AI. But for people with privacy concerns, the only way to opt out of this was to delete your entire chat history. Now, Google is overhauling the process to eliminate that drawback.

Also: I checked Gemini’s fresh Memory summary to see what it knew about me.

Sources indicate that in a change set to roll out in the coming weeks, you’ll be able to put the brakes on Gemini model training without losing access to your previous conversations with the AI. Here’s how this works now — and how it will work down the road.

Sources indicate that right now, Gemini offers a setting called Keep Activity that controls not only whether and for how long your chats are saved but also whether they’re used to train the AI. You can’t separate the two.

To correct this problem, Google will replace Keep Activity with two new settings. With the first setting, you’ll be able to keep or delete your past chats and choose how long your history will be saved. With the second setting, you’ll be able to decide whether your chats, including all text and attachments, will be used for model training.

Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes.

“With this change, you will be able to keep your history while independently controlling generative AI model training,” Google said in an announcement shared to Gemini users via email.

Here’s how this will play out. If your Keep Activity setting is off when this change is made, both new settings will be off. If your Keep Activity setting is on, both new settings will be on. That means you’ll need to head to Gemini’s Settings if you wish to opt out of model training but still be able to view and access your previous chats.

Almost all AIs include a setting for model training that you typically have to manually disable if you’re concerned about your privacy. But most let you opt out without turning off your chat history.

Industry observers note that chatGPT offers a setting called “Improve the model for everyone,” which is double-speak for model training. But this is easy enough to turn off. Microsoft Copilot provides settings for “Training on conversation activity” and “Training on voice conversations,” both of which you can disable to opt out of model training. Claude’s AI training option is turned off by default. But you can always control this by checking the setting for “Help improve our AI models.”.

Also: 5 ways AI will change how you defend your business in 2027.

In all those cases, you still retain access to your conversation history. In contrast, Google has been the only AI player among the majors to impose a restriction for those who want to opt out of AI training. Based on past actions, Google has often earned a reputation for being privacy-unfriendly. I’m glad to see the company take this step in the right direction.

#39198. Not Safe, Not Creative: 123456 Is Still the World’s Most Common Password

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (909 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Not Safe, Not Creative: 123456 Is Still the World’s Most Common Password

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (909 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Our data keeps getting hacked, breached, stolen and exposed, and yet we’re still using the most predictable passwords.
  • For the seventh time in the past eight years, 123456 is the world’s most common password, and it’s got other uncreative companions on the list, according to the latest analysis by password and passkey manager NordPass, a division of Nord Security.
  • Sources indicate that in the 44 countries analyzed, the password 123456 was used more than 7.2 million times.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Our data keeps getting hacked, breached, stolen and exposed, and yet we’re still using the most predictable passwords.

For the seventh time in the past eight years, 123456 is the world’s most common password, and it’s got other uncreative companions on the list, according to the latest analysis by password and passkey manager NordPass, a division of Nord Security. The top three most used passwords in the US were: 123456, password and admin. Yikes.

Sources indicate that in the 44 countries analyzed, the password 123456 was used more than 7.2 million times. The rest of the top 10 passwords: admin, 12345678, 123456789, 1234, 12345, password, Aa123456, Pass@123 and 1234567890.

Industry observers note that nordPass remarked that even though many people prefer simple, easy-to-remember passwords, much more awareness of password safety is needed. The company recommends creating a unique password for each account that’s at least 15 characters long, including uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers and special characters. Though it’s tempting to reuse the same passwords, hackers rely on that complacency.

Industry observers note that nordPass suggests upgrading weak, old passwords to stronger ones. You can also add multifactor authentication, which requires an additional layer of security beyond a login password. That could mean entering a one-time passcode sent by text or email, answering security questions, or using facial recognition or fingerprint ID.

Industry observers note that CNET managing editor Adam Benjamin stated that the risk isn’t primarily from someone randomly guessing your password. The danger is from algorithms that collect data or bots that use credential stuffing (in other words, stolen username and password pairs obtained from a data breach).

Sources indicate that according to Benjamin, using an obscure reference or a different language doesn’t make a password stronger. “A password is good when it’s too much trouble for an algorithm to crack,” he said.

You might remember the scene from the 1987 movie Spaceballs, where the combination to Planet Druidia’s air shield is 12345. Dark Helmet calls it “the stupidest combination I’ve ever heard in my life!” and indicates it’s “the kind of thing an idiot would have on his luggage.” The joke remains a staple reference for weak passwords and PINs, and yet, here we are.

Last year, two researchers hacked into McDonald’s hiring chatbot by guessing the password 123456 to access 64 million data records, including applicant names, email addresses and phone numbers.

It has been revealed that in 2023, the Akira ransomware group hacked into KNP Logistics Group, a 158‑year‑old UK transportation firm, by guessing an employee’s weak password. The hackers locked the company’s data and demanded a $6.6 million ransom, forcing KNP to shut down and lay off 700 workers.

This year, suspected Iranian hackers gained access to US water supply systems due to internet-connected devices that used default passwords — or none at all.

According to recent reports, the rise of the AI era has also made password hacking easier. One study even found that some AI systems could determine people’s passwords by listening to their keystrokes.

Recent findings suggest that nordPass has conducted its Top 200 Most Common Passwords analysis since 2019. To compile its lists, NordPass and independent researchers examined passwords exposed in public data breaches and dark web repositories, then organized and categorized the data by country of origin.

Industry observers note that nordPass has found that password habits are heavily influenced by current trends and culture. Over the last several years, some of the top three passwords have been Lebron0319 (in reference to NBA star LeBron James), Savage20 (musical group) and roblox.com1 (video game). In the 2010s, the top three were Lachimolala (meme), telegram (social media) and minecraft (video game).

It has been revealed that but while these passwords might make us feel nostalgic for these time capsules of experiences, interests and entertainment, they don’t translate to strong internet security. “Unfortunately, fandoms make for terrible passwords,” the NordPass report notes.

Passwords based on pop culture, current events and sports can be easily predicted or cracked in seconds using automated tools, especially if your interests are visible on public social media profiles. Adding a number to the end of a password doesn’t help — attackers program their tools to test common number combinations and symbol swaps.

Given all the accounts we deal with — financial institutions, social media, stores, government agencies — creating dozens of unique passwords and remembering them can be exhausting and annoying.

“Inventing passwords that meet that criterion across hundreds of logins is virtually impossible, which is why we recommend password managers to create long, complex passwords and then store them all for you,” remarked Benjamin.

In a recent development, A password manager creates and updates passwords for apps, Wi-Fi networks and websites, ensuring that all your passwords are unique and resistant to bot attacks. Another plus is that you don’t have to remember them or write them down: They’re stored in an encrypted vault you can access by verifying your identity. Password managers can also auto-fill login credentials.

Sources indicate that CNET senior writer Joe Supan said the best password managers also offer passkeys, which are ways of logging into apps and websites using biometric ID, such as facial or fingerprint scans, or PIN codes. “These are really the sign-in methods of the future, and I probably wouldn’t recommend a password manager that doesn’t include them at this point,” Supan said.

CNET’s top two recommendations for password managers are NordPass and Bitwarden.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Physical media lovers, take note: Best Buy has begun selling 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray discs in-store and online.
  • Now, thanks to Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster phenom and Oscar frontrunner The Odyssey, which is the first-ever movie to be filmed entirely on IMAX cameras, the firm is once again stocking its shelves with Blu-rays.
  • But this move also raises the question: Will other 4K and standard Blu-rays be coming to Best Buy stores in the near future?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Physical media lovers, take note: Best Buy has begun selling 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray discs in-store and online. If you’ve been paying attention, you’ll know how substantial a pivot this is for the electronics retailer. Back in 2023, the tech giant confirmed it would cease all sales of DVDs and Blu-rays entirely.

Now, thanks to Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster phenom and Oscar frontrunner The Odyssey, which is the first-ever movie to be filmed entirely on IMAX cameras, the firm is once again stocking its shelves with Blu-rays. Right now, you’ll find only copies of the Greek epic in store (with a small selection of other titles available for purchase directly through the retailer’s online store), and that makes sense considering how popular it was in theaters and how awesome it will look on major TVs at home.

But this move also raises the question: Will other 4K and standard Blu-rays be coming to Best Buy stores in the near future?

A Best Buy spokesperson didn’t immediately reply to our request for comment.

When the retailer first confirmed it would be ditching DVD and Blu-ray sales, it cited the decades-long decline in physical media sales — which fell from its peak revenue benchmark of $16 billion in 2005 to less than $1 billion in 2024 — and planned to populate the store space with other tech-based products.

The Odyssey, the nearly 3-hour-long massive-screen adaptation of Homer’s epic poem, follows King Odysseus (played by Matt Damon) as he leads his soldiers on a 10-year journey home after the Trojan War. It features a stacked slate of acting talent from Anne Hathaway and Tom Holland to Zendaya, Jon Bernthal and Charlize Theron, and earned $1.8 billion at the global box office.

Those details, along with the timing of the coming holiday shopping season, have apparently inspired Best Buy to change course.

On Monday, Google rolled out an M157 update for the Chrome web browser on Googlebook OS, with a handful of new features and performance boosts to streamline your workflow and browsing experience.

While the first Googlebooks on the market have received mixed reviews, these features could help the laptops gain more useful features in Chrome that other browsers already offer.

Here are the five fresh Chrome features on Googlebook OS to know about.

Industry observers note that if you’ve ever had to share your screen on a video call, you know how irritating it can be to switch tabs without having to repeatedly start and stop sharing. This Chrome revision adds a tab-sharing controls bar; when you share a browser tab in a video call, Chrome will display a persistent control bar at the top of the window so you can “Stop sharing” or “Share this tab instead” from any tab.

Also: 6 Chrome default settings I changed to instantly.

When you hover over a collapsed vertical tab rail with your mouse or trackpad, it will expand, so you can read full tab titles, switch tabs, or manage groups. The rail will collapse again when you move the cursor away.

In a recent development, this auto-expand feature is enabled by default. If you want to turn it off or on, go to Settings > Appearance > Tab position > “Auto expand tabs on hover,” or right-click the vertical tab rail.

According to recent reports, the Chrome upgrade allows you to manually resize your vertical tab bar to view longer page titles when needed. The browser will remember your custom tab width, even after you open a new window or restart the browser. (You’ll just need to turn “Auto expand tabs on hover” off for it to work.).

You can now save individual Chrome Settings subpages as direct web addresses that you can type, bookmark, or link to directly (for example, chrome://settings/privacy), meaning you won’t have to go digging around in menus to change your preferences anymore. You can navigate between these Settings subpages with the Back and Forward buttons.

The system’s “Save As” file picker is now enabled by default for menu save actions, such as “Save link as” and “Save image as,” so you can more easily rename files and select a destination folder. This includes Google Drive or external storage.

It has been revealed that also: Google Chrome running slow? 5 easy ways to speed it up fast.

Outside of these upcoming features, a few of Chrome M157’s performance fixes include the ability to press Ctrl+L to reveal and select web addresses; keeping your bookmarks bar visible in fullscreen mode and while screen sharing; better media controls while using Picture-in-Picture mode; and the ability to partially translate PDFs within your browser.

If you have Chrome set up to automatically download and install updates, you won’t have to lift a finger to take advantage of the fresh features and performance boosts.

But if you’ve disabled automatic updates, you can manually upgrade by selecting the three-dot menu in the top-right corner of your Chrome window and navigating to Help > About Google Chrome > Relaunch.

Also: My week with new Googlebooks: The good, the bad, and the promising.

Sources indicate that if the Relaunch option is greyed out or nowhere to be found, you’re running on the latest version of Chrome. And if you were working on something before the patch, don’t worry: Chrome will save your open tabs and reopen them automatically when you restart.

💡 Key Takeaways
